rows.old_text: # Moldova company formation and entity choice, 2026 v0.8
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ## Who this applies to
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Use this Guide to prepare an ordinary Moldovan SRL incorporation, compare the individual-entrepreneur registration route and screen an SA proposal. It supplies the current registration and continuing-compliance framework as read on 30 October 2026. It does not certify the full securities-registration procedure, regulated-sector approvals, every foreign-document treaty exemption or historical incorporation rules throughout 2026. The bounded source-review record is linked under Sources. [Law 135/2007 arts. 2, 9, 11–16][srl]; [Law 220/2007 arts. 7–14, 28, 35][register]; [Law 1134/1997 arts. 2–4, 38][sa].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: An SRL has legal personality and capital divided into participation interests. It is formed on State registration; the company answers with its assets, while members' liability has the exceptions in article 9, including unpaid subscribed contributions. One or more permitted individuals or legal entities can found it. An SA divides capital into shares and has its own company/securities requirements. An individual entrepreneur registers the individual under Law 220 article 28. These legal choices do not themselves prove entitlement to a tax incentive. Do not describe one as universally best, safest or most common without evidence about the proposed business. [Law 135 arts. 2, 9, 11][srl]; [Law 1134 arts. 2–4][sa]; [Law 220 art. 28][register].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: An ordinary SRL has no general numerical member cap. The article-11(4) exception limits a qualifying crowdfunding investment vehicle to **200 members**. A company board is compulsory with **more than 50 members**; at **50 members or fewer** the statute can provide for one. Build the actual governance arrangement into the statute rather than treating every multi-member SRL identically. [Law 135 arts. 11, 63][srl].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The published agency fee is not a quotation for legal advice, translation, apostille, name services, bank charges or every ancillary service. ASP's relief footnote names Law 220 article 4, SME Law 179/2016 article 15, Law 39/2006 article 3 and Government Decision 707/2025 point 2. The sourced statutory relief categories are explained below; the remaining programme/first-year evidence and unquoted service routes are not established here. Law 220 article 4(1) permits Government-set electronic/counter tariffs within the annex ceiling; use the current service and applicant category, not the old approximate “under 1,500” estimate. [Law 220 art. 4][register]; [ASP tariff and relief footnote][asp].

rows.old_text: The name-service table’s **five working days / free** track is tied to Noncommercial Organisations Law 86/2020 article 13(4)–(5). For organisations within that law’s scope, a founder requests name-availability confirmation by email or in person before registration, and the registrar responds within **five working days**. The name is reserved on request for **six months without a fee**. Article 13(3) separately makes registration and statute changes fee-free for those noncommercial organisations. These rules do not create unconditional free or urgent service for every commercial company. Choose the actual entity/channel, term and relief rather than adding alternative tariffs together. [Law 86 arts. 1, 13(3)–(5)][noncommercial]; [ASP name-service table and footnote][aspname].

rows.old_text: ### Apply only the relief matching the applicant and service
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Law 220 article 4(2) makes **re-registration required by a change in legislation free**. Its one-stop rule puts the specified one-stop services within the registration fee without extra applicant charges; it is not an exemption from that fee for every new business. A motivated registration refusal does not make the payment refundable under article 4(8). [Law 220 art. 4(2), (4)–(5), (8)][register].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The **debutant enterprise** relief under SME Law 179/2016 article 15 is conditional. The company must be an SRL, meet that law’s microenterprise category, be founded and administered by natural persons aged **18–35 inclusive at registration** carrying on economic activity through an SRL for the first time, and have **no more than five members**. Article 3 separately defines a newly registered enterprise by the **one-year** period from establishment. Article 15(1) describes support for **three years from State registration**, while paragraph (3)(a) expressly exempts qualifying debutants from State-registration and information-supply fees. Paragraph (4) leaves further support-instrument benefits/obligations to the Government; this Guide does not certify an unverified programme application or every urgent-service entitlement. [Law 179 arts. 3, 15][smerelief]; [ASP relief footnote][asp].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For this **SME-law** classification in 2026, article 5(1)(a) requires **at most nine employees** and annual net turnover **not above EUR 2 million equivalent in MDL, or total assets not above EUR 2 million equivalent in MDL**. Use the average annual exchange rate for the calculation year under article 4(3). Article 5 uses average annual staff and its own financial-category/reclassification rules; movement from a smaller into a larger category requires failure of the smaller category in **two consecutive financial years**. These current limits apply from **1 January 2026** under the amendments displayed in articles 4–5. They are not the Accounting Law’s reporting-category thresholds or automatic entitlement to the corporate **4%** tax regime. Actual first-year eligibility evidence, any further Government support-instrument conditions and handling of the urgent track remain separate checks. [Law 179 arts. 4–5, 15][smerelief]; [Accounting Law art. 4][accounts]; [corporate-income Guide](md-corporate-income-tax.md).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Law 39/2006 article 3(1)(b) supplies a separate State-registration/constituting-document-change fee exemption for residents of its **specified Dubăsari economic zone**. Article 1 lists Cocieri/Vasilievca, Corjova/Mahala, Coșnița/Pohrebea, Molovata Nouă/Roghi, Doroțcaia and Pîrîta. Article 2 requires the individual’s domicile there, or the legal entity’s office **and** production/service activity there. Do not extend that population to every Moldovan or Transnistrian applicant. The provision’s historic **2006–2010** income-tax exemption is not a 2026 exemption; other special-zone tax interactions and implementing evidence are not certified by this formation-fee analysis. [Law 39 arts. 1–3, especially 3(1)(b)][zone39]; [ASP relief footnote][asp].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Government Decision 966/2020, latest displayed operative consolidation effective **15 October 2026**, approves the tariff and relief schedules. Enacted **HG 707/2025 point 2** specifically makes registration/update of company or individual-entrepreneur beneficial-owner data **free on an electronic application**, within the period in Law 220 article 5(2): **24 hours on a working day, calculated from the following working day after the necessary documents are presented**. Point 3.3 sets technical-readiness commencement, **no later than 1 December 2025**. This is a specific beneficial-owner service, not free incorporation or a substitute deadline for every ordinary individual-register change; article 29 retains its three-working-day decision rule for that ordinary change procedure. Keep the client’s obligation to submit changed ownership data within 30 days separate from the authority’s service clock. [HG 707 points 2, 3.3][hg707]; [Law 220 arts. 5(2), 29][register]; [Law 308 art. 14][aml]; [Government Decision 966 points 1–2][tariff966].

rows.old_text: ## The base
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Prepare the SRL decision, statute and contributions
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Identify founders, proposed name and registered office, actual activities and any required permit, administrator, representation and governance, subscribed capital, each participation interest, contribution type and payment schedule. The full name includes the Romanian legal form and the abbreviated name `S.R.L.`. The statute is approved and signed by all founders or authorised persons and is prepared in Romanian. Its required contents are in article 13, including the founding persons, business activity, capital and interests, contribution method/deadline, office, governing bodies, representation and reorganisation/liquidation arrangements. [Law 135 arts. 3–5, 11–14][srl].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Cash is the presumed contribution unless the statute provides otherwise. Permitted contributions include property, property/intellectual-property rights and money. For in-kind contributions, the statute sets how the members approve the valuation results; ownership passes to the company unless the statute provides otherwise. Members cannot simply demand return of paid-in capital while the company operates. Record amounts subscribed, paid and outstanding separately; a nominal capital entry does not prove payment or satisfy all creditor protections. [Law 135 arts. 21–23][srl].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: If State registration has not occurred within **three months from approval of the statute**, Law 135 article 16(3) applies Civil Code article 248(2) correspondingly. The current Civil Code gives the founders the **right to be released from obligations arising from their subscriptions unless the constituting act provides otherwise**. Its general trigger is approval of that act by all founders. Record the actual approval and all-founder decision, the elapsed period and the constituting act’s terms before applying the right; do not label it automatic cancellation of every contribution or replace approval with an old notarisation/signing-date summary. This concerns failure to register, separately from a registered SRL’s six-month contribution obligation. The Civil Code version read is effective **1 April 2026**, not the displayed future 2027 versions. [Law 135 art. 16(3), 22][srl]; [Civil Code arts. 246–248, especially 248(2)][civil].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Check founder and administrator eligibility separately
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Law 220 article 13(1)(g) bars registration when the enterprise’s founder has **unspent convictions for tax evasion**. Other grounds in article 13 remain separate, including a registration prohibition by a court, enforcement officer or competent authority, and the specified three-year restriction for a founder of an entity deregistered under Fiscal Code article 174^1. A truthful tax-evasion declaration does not override those other grounds. [Law 220 art. 13(1), (2), (4)–(5)][register].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ASP’s actual **7-16** blank declaration identifies the declarant by name/IDNP **as founder** of the named entity, states that the declarant has no unspent tax-evasion convictions, and requires date/signature. ASP labels **7-17** “Administrator şi fondator”; it records both an administrator capacity and a founder capacity with separate entity-name fields. Complete the actual capacities, entity or entities and authority; do not assume those fields establish the ownership/representation relationship or automatically make the declarant the new company’s administrator. These two one-page templates were retrieved, read and visually inspected. A signed blank-template statement is not an official criminal-record finding, proof of expungement or a general administrator-clearance certificate. [Founder declaration 7-16][founderconviction]; [administrator/founder declaration 7-17][entityfounderconviction]; [ASP linked templates][asp].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: An SRL’s natural-person administrator must have full legal capacity, no statutory or judicial prohibition on holding the administrator or other relevant asset-disposal position, and **no unspent convictions in the categories specified by article 69(2)**: offences against property, economic offences, and offences committed by responsible officials or persons managing commercial organisations. That test is wider than the founder form’s tax-evasion statement. An administrator can be a member or a third party; appointment is by the members’ meeting or, if the statute so provides, the board. Submit the appointment/removal and identity for State registration with the relevant decision. With several administrators, representation powers are equal unless the statute provides otherwise. [Law 135 arts. 69–71][srl].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The statute can permit a **legal entity** to be administrator under article 69(2^1). Civil Code article 199 then requires it to designate **one natural person** to exercise the function permanently. That person must meet the legal administrator requirements, has the same obligations and is jointly liable with the legal-entity administrator. Revoking that person does not take effect until a replacement is appointed; designation/revocation follows the administrator-publicity formalities using the legal entity’s decision. Preserve both layers of authority and the actual eligibility evidence. Do not infer eligibility solely because the application has a legal-person branch. [Law 135 art. 69(2^1)][srl]; [Civil Code art. 199][civil].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Assemble and submit the registration file
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text:
1. Check the name and office. For online submission, verify name availability before filing. The current ASP commercial-company service requires a reserved name and electronic signatures on all attached documents; its online route is offered for SRLs and SAs. Match the name certificate and actual channel requirements. [ASP selected SRL service][asp]; [company instructions points 4, 9–10][companyinstructions]. The registered office is entered from the constituting documents; article 10 places responsibility for authenticity on the entity and does not authorise a universal extra premises-proof demand. [Law 220 arts. 9–10][register].
2. Obtain the registration application signed by the founder designated in the formation decision or the person authorised there, the decision and constituting documents approved by the founders, beneficial-owner information, the SA registrar information where relevant, and any additional act/opinion required by the applicable law. For a regulated field, the application declares the required prior approval and the registrar checks it through the prescribed data exchange. Beneficial-owner disclosure is required by article 7(1)(f); apply the statutory ownership and disclosure method below, rather than naming every shareholder or defaulting to the administrator. [Law 220 art. 7(1)–(1^1)][register].
3. For a foreign legal-entity investment, obtain the relevant registry extract and foreign constituting documents. Article 8(2^1) requires authorised Romanian translation and the applicable legalisation/apostille route, subject to actual treaty exemptions. Verify the document's origin and treaty rather than assuming all foreign or CIS documents are exempt. [Law 220 arts. 7(4), 8(2^1)][register].
4. Submit Romanian documents electronically with the prescribed electronic signatures, on paper at the registrar or by registered post. A representative needs the legally valid authenticated power or qualifying electronic-register authorisation. The registrar can obtain official electronic information directly where article 8 permits; keep the receipt listing the application number/date, submitted documents and planned release date. [Law 220 art. 8][register].
5. Pay the applicable registration charge and retain the complete-payment confirmation. Processing follows payment as specified in article 7(5). The registrar checks the file and issues registration or a reasoned refusal. Preserve the decision, statute and register information; the assigned **IDNO is also the entity's fiscal code**. The one-stop procedure transmits registration data for tax, statistical, medical and social records and gives the prescribed notice. This transmission does not prove a separate VAT-registration entitlement or fulfil every later filing. [Law 220 arts. 7(5), 11, 14][register]; [VAT Code art. 112][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For individual-entrepreneur registration, article 28 prescribes the application, article-8 submission route, identity/capacity verification and one-stop notifications. Do not apply the company statute/capital checklist mechanically to an individual. A person already registered as an individual entrepreneur, or judicially disqualified from the activity, engages article 30's refusal conditions. The current individual tariff and the ordinary application fields are supplied below; profession-specific authorisations remain separate. [Law 220 arts. 28–30][register].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Complete the actual company application and formation declaration
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The current ASP SRL checklist links application **3-5**, its completion instructions and the founding documents. Its two application pages and all five instruction pages were retrieved and visually inspected. Reconcile the application, formation decision, statute, capital/ownership schedule and actual signatories before submission. The selected checklist also requires beneficial-owner information and the specified self-declaration concerning unextinguished tax-evasion convictions; choose the actual founder/administrator role and applicable current form. The role-specific conviction declaration and separate administrator eligibility tests are mapped above; case-specific criminal-record expiry, rehabilitation and foreign-record recognition are not determined by a blank form. [ASP selected SRL checklist][asp]; [application][companyform]; [instructions][companyinstructions]; [Law 220 arts. 7–8][register].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text:
| Application fields | Completion method |
|---|---|
| Date, requested service, fields 1–5 | Actual filing date and requested 24-hour/four-hour track; full name matching the reservation certificate, abbreviated name, full legal form, actual fixed/unlimited duration, registered office and valid contacts |
| Administrator, field 6 | Complete the natural-person or legal-person branch as applicable. For a legal-person administrator, provide its current registry/foreign-registry data and the natural representative’s identity. Record the actual appointment term; the form does not itself authorise every administrator arrangement |

rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Application 3-5 acknowledges one-stop registration and repeats a **30-day** company register-change undertaking. It does not prove that an actual company has been registered, that a licence has been granted or that every later tax/accounting obligation is fulfilled. Distinguish ordinary company changes measured from the decision under Law 220 article 16 from beneficial-owner updates measured from the change under Law 308 article 14. [Application page 2][companyform]; [instructions points 6–24][companyinstructions]; [Law 220 art. 16][register]; [Law 308 art. 14][aml].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For formation, the ASP checklist identifies **BE-1 for an individual founder** and **BE-2 for a legal-entity founder**. Each founder, or its properly authorised representative, submits its own signed declaration at constitution. After constitution, ASP’s published procedure names the administrator or designated resident natural person as signer. The actual BE-1 and BE-2 core forms, **pages 1–2 of each**, were read and visually inspected; their five-page PEP annexes were not fully verified. [ASP checklist][asp]; [ASP signer guidance][bofaq]; [BE-1][companybe1]; [BE-2][companybe2].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: BE-1 records the individual founder and its interest; BE-2 records the founding entity, its administrator and the ownership chain. Follow that chain to natural persons and retain the actual supporting evidence. Both forms distinguish identified beneficial owners and control through other means from the conditional administrator fallback. Complete the applicable identity/interest/control and PEP sections, annex list, signature and date; unused fields are crossed out as the notes require. The notes request interests to **two decimal places**; this presentation rule does not decide the statutory threshold or permit exclusion of other control. Foreign-document legalisation, travel-document evidence and treaty exceptions still require their actual applicable route. [BE-1/BE-2 core pages and notes][companybe1]; [BE-2][companybe2]; [Law 308 art. 5^2][aml]; [Law 220 arts. 7–8][register].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Identify the beneficial owner and keep the correct update clock
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Use **Law 308 of 22 December 2017**, current consolidation amended by Law 146/2026 effective **13 August 2026**. Its publication date in 2018 does not change the enactment year. The agency’s individual-service “308/2018” reference and older application footnotes do not replace the current statute. [Current Law 308 heading, arts. 5^2, 8^1, 14][aml].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For an ordinary private commercial company, article 5^2 identifies the natural person who ultimately owns/controls the client or on whose behalf/in whose interest the activity or transaction occurs. Test direct/indirect ownership and control through other means. **25% plus one share**, or **more than 25% of capital**, are the stated ownership indicators; exactly 25% does not itself meet the capital indicator, and a lower holding does not exclude control through other means. The administrator fallback applies only after exhausting all possible means, no owner/controller being identified and no grounds for suspicion. Record the work and evidence; do not automatically list the administrator because a corporate shareholder or fragmented ownership makes tracing inconvenient. Trusts, noncommercial bodies and other legal structures have article 5^2(2)’s own categories. [Law 308 art. 5^2(1)–(2)][aml].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Article 14 requires adequate, accurate, current beneficial-owner information and benefit-interest details. Companies and individual entrepreneurs designate a **resident natural person** responsible for providing/updating it. Submit beneficial-owner changes to ASP within **30 days from the change**, as article 14(2) and ASP’s specific guidance expressly state for both populations. This is separate from an individual entrepreneur’s ordinary **three-day** register-data-change duty and a company’s ordinary 30-day-from-decision duty. If an event also changes other register data, schedule every required filing and meet the earliest applicable duty; do not delay an ordinary individual-register change until the beneficial-owner deadline. [Law 308 art. 14(2), (2^1), (3^1)][aml]; [ASP specific beneficial-owner deadline][bofaq]; [Law 220 arts. 16, 29][register].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ASP’s beneficial-owner register duty has article 14(1)’s exclusions for public institutions/authorities, State/municipal enterprises and wholly or majority State-owned companies. Ordinary private SRL registration is prohibited without beneficial-owner data or with false/incomplete information under article 14(3). A filed declaration is therefore neither optional nor proof that the ownership analysis was correct. [Law 308 art. 14(1), (3)][aml].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ASP publishes an electronic filing route through RSUD, using Romanian electronic documents and the prescribed qualified electronic signatures. Its guidance says to complete the system fields, attach the appropriate signed declaration/supporting documents, sign the generated request and finalise the order. The published online beneficial-owner service is free; the counter service uses the applicable statutory tariff. Save the actual submission and acceptance/registration evidence. These are read agency instructions, not a portal test or a filed application; the ordinary company/individual post-formation applications and declarations are mapped below; the actual discrepancy-removal procedure remains a separate check. [ASP channels, online steps and signer guidance][bofaq]; [Law 220 art. 8][register].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### File post-formation ownership and register changes
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Select the application and the separate beneficial-owner declaration by legal form and filing event. ASP’s current catalogue identifies **3-11** for company beneficial-owner register changes, **3-22** for individual-entrepreneur register changes, and **BE-3** for a company after constitution, including changes, reorganisations and deregistration. **BE-4 is for noncommercial constitution**; it is not the company’s post-formation declaration. Individual entrepreneurs use **BE-8**. [ASP catalogue][boforms]; [company application][companyupdate]; [individual application][iiupdate]; [BE-3][companybe3].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For company application 3-11, enter the actual filing date, registered full name, IDNO and its date, requested **24-hour/four-hour** service, each natural beneficial owner’s identity-document/birth/citizenship/domicile/residence/contact data, and the percentage held or controlled. List the actual supporting documents and sign as administrator or lawful representative; collective administration follows the authority in the constituting document. Instructions 6–12 require applicable fields, valid identity data and article-17 supporting documents. Their ordinary 24-hour working-day clock starts on the working day following presentation of the necessary documents; it does not promise same-calendar-day completion. The application’s contact and signature fields must also be completed. [3-11 application][companyupdate]; [instructions points 6–12][companyupdateinstructions]; [Law 220 arts. 16–17][register].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Keep registration disclosure separate from bank and adviser due diligence
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Identify the party owing the duty. Banks and the other entities in Law 308 article 4, including its specified professional/accounting/tax-advice populations, have customer-due-diligence duties; registration does not make every ordinary private company a reporting entity. At the start of a business relationship, the reporting entity verifies customer identity from reliable independent sources, identifies/verifies the natural beneficial owner and ownership/control structure, checks representatives’ identity/authority, understands purpose/nature and performs ongoing monitoring. Clients provide the required evidence and update changed beneficial-owner information. Article 14(8) prohibits exclusive reliance on registrar data. An ASP extract therefore does not guarantee that a bank will open an account. Actual bank procedures and risk decisions remain case-specific. [Law 308 arts. 4, 5(1)(a), (2), (5), (7), 14(8)][aml].

The forms’ lookback question does not certify automatic risk expiry or replace that assessment. rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Missing required documents, non-compliant constitution, statutory restrictions and the other article-13 grounds can produce a reasoned registration refusal. The registrar cannot refuse merely for inexpediency; after curing the grounds the applicant can reapply, and refusal can be challenged in court. Article 4(8) states the prescribed non-refund rule. False formation information engages Law 135 article 19's joint liability, subject to its knowledge condition; failure to pay a subscribed contribution engages article 9(4) and article 22. General registration/accounting breaches carry the liability specified by the applicable law. This Guide supplies no invented universal registration fine. Tax late charges and filing sanctions follow the relevant tax Guide and actual debt. [Law 220 arts. 4(8), 13, 38][register]; [Law 135 arts. 9, 19, 22][srl]; [Accounting Law art. 34][accounts].

rows.old_text: ## Who this applies to
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Compute ordinary resident-company profit tax and the separate eligible non-VAT SME income regime for 2026. Establish the taxpayer, elected regime and applicable period before calculating. Resident business entities include income from Moldova and abroad, less the deductions and exemptions they actually qualify for. Legal persons use accrual accounting. This is a source-cited draft, without accountant attestation or comprehensive country coverage. [Fiscal Code arts. 13–14, 44][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: A company is resident if its activity is organised or managed in Moldova, or Moldova is its principal place of activity. The ordinary income-tax period is the calendar year; a newly created business starts at registration. A lawful noncalendar accounting period has Code art. 12^1(4)–(6)'s separate eligibility, notification and transition requirements; liquidation, reorganisation and IT-park entry/exit have their own short-period rules. Do not use the excise article 121 in place of income-tax article 12^1. [Code arts. 5(5)(b), 12^1][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The 7% rate belongs to the statutory **gospodărie țărănească (de fermier)** category. It is not a rate for every agricultural company. Individual entrepreneurs use the 12% annual taxable-income rule and their own personal/entity procedures; the corporate Guide does not replace the [individual-income Guide](moldova-income-tax.md). IT-park, free-zone, financial-sector and other special regimes require their own legal eligibility tests. Use [transfer pricing](md-transfer-pricing.md), [cross-border](md-cross-border.md), [VAT](moldova-vat.md), [payroll](moldova-payroll.md) and [social contributions](moldova-social-contributions.md) for the connected subjects, with each file's stated currency and gaps. [Arts. 15, 49, 54^1, 87(1^1)][code].

Do not use the latter date for the SME threshold or confuse the SME test with VAT registration. The change is a regime-eligibility/election rule, not a daily apportionment of the 4% rate. [Law 41 arts. I(1), I(4), X][amend].

rows.old_text: ## The base
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text:
1. **Choose and document the regime.** Article 54^1 excludes VAT-registered taxpayers, peasant farms, individual entrepreneurs and the specified consultancy-heavy businesses from the SME class. For the election cases, test prior 31 December income from exempt-without-credit supplies alone or together with taxable supplies, the applicable threshold and the requirement that exempt-without-credit supplies exceed 50% of total supplies. No-prior-income and newly registered entities have separate election routes. Record the choice in accounting policy by 25 April for the first two routes, or by the 25th of the month after the registration quarter for new entities. Test the shareholding/number-of-SMEs limit. VAT registration moves the taxpayer to general taxation from registration; cancellation uses the art. 113(4) date. Preserve each regime's actual tax period. [Arts. 54^1–54^1/1][code].
2. **Reconcile ordinary profit tax.** Start with accounting revenue and expenses, not bank deposits. Include the taxable art. 18 receipts, including business receipts, rent, interest, royalties, covered debt releases and non-exempt subsidies/penal receipts. Remove only income demonstrably exempt under art. 20 or another controlling rule. Resident-company dividends received from another resident company have art. 20(z^19)'s exemption except the specified undistributed 2008–2011 profits. Recovery/reversal of an expense or provision never deducted has art. 20(z^17)'s rule, with its exception for provisions created in the stated 2023–2026 deferral periods. Do not exempt every grant, compensation or revaluation without its precise statutory category. Reconcile timing, unpaid related-party amounts and prior-year returns/discounts under art. 44. Add back income tax, statutory fines/penalties, private or exempt-income expenditure, unsupported related payments and other disallowed costs. Do not deduct a capital-asset purchase as an ordinary expense when depreciation rules apply. [Arts. 18, 20, 24, 30, 44][code].
3. **Apply expense-specific limits.** Ordinary necessary business expenses qualify under art. 24(1). Mixed business/private costs require its actual greater-business-than-private test and only the directly business portion. Travel, representation and business insurance have Government limits; do not assume the accounting amount qualifies. One-car restrictions apply to the specified occupation groups 112/121. Related-party losses need the arm's-length exception or other stated exception. Undocumented ordinary expenses have the 0.2%-of-taxable-income route; business-card purchases have a separate rule. Patent-holder/independent-retailer payments have their own restriction. Membership/subscription and qualifying union allocations have the separate 0.15%-of-payroll or two-forecast-average-salaries limit; the exact applicable alternative and recipient must be documented. [Art. 24(1)–(11)][code].
4. **Check new service-entrepreneur payments.** The art. 24(11^1) route covers the specified businesses with at most 9 employees and turnover or assets up to 18 million, subject to its 10%-of-annual-payroll payment limit, or the separate main-activity route above 70% for CAEM 59.1, 90.01, 90.02, 93.11 or 93.12. Verify the exact route rather than deducting every freelancer invoice. Employment reclassification and the recipient's separate single-tax regime must also be checked in the payroll/individual work. [Art. 24(11^1)][code]; [Finance Ministry 2026 explanation][changes].
5. **Reconcile employee-related expenditure.** Article 24(19^3) provides: annual in-kind gifts/vouchers up to 10% of the forecast monthly average salary per employee; specified training/team-building up to 5% of the defined payroll fund after excluding the stated management groups; sport subscriptions and qualifying rural-tourism/vacation-voucher costs together up to 50% of the forecast average salary per employee; medical services up to one forecast average salary per employee. Article 24(20) separately covers qualifying voluntary medical-insurance premiums up to one forecast average salary. The 2026 forecast is 17,400, giving 1,740, 8,700 and 17,400 for those respective per-employee caps. Taxed compensation above those limits must be tested under art. 24(19^2), not automatically disallowed or treated as exempt remuneration. Childcare has its separate 2,500-per-month-per-child limit for children under 3. Preserve the actual provider, benefit, cumulative-period and payroll facts. [Art. 24(19)–(20), (26)][code]; [CNAS 2026 instructions, point 12.1, citing Government Decision 773/2025][average].
6. **Financing, depreciation and other deductions.** For loans from the specified non-financial individuals/entities, compare the actual contractual interest with the BNM weighted banking rate for the matching currency and term, up to or above 12 months. Keep that limit distinct from transfer pricing. Maintain each tangible asset separately; ordinary straight-line depreciation starts the month after commissioning, using the Government useful life. Financial versus operating leasing determines the depreciating party, with the stated IFRS right-of-use exception. For qualifying repairs to rented/leased assets outside the ownership test, the ordinary limit is 15% of accrued rent/operating-lease/concession consideration; international aircraft have the separate 100% operating-lease cap, and qualifying own taxi vehicles have the stated full-repair deduction. Free assets are not depreciated unless their value entered taxable income; non-taxable partial financing limits the depreciable part, subject to the statutory post-investment subsidy exception. The non-financial-sector accelerated option permits at most 50% of entry cost in the first year, followed by remaining value over remaining useful life. Financial/operating leases, IFRS right-of-use assets, rented-asset repairs, grants and disposals each have separate rules. Limited-life intangibles amortise straight-line. Ordinary provisions and revaluation/impairment do not become deductible merely because booked; a legally established business bad debt has its own rule. [Arts. 25, 26^1, 28, 31][code].
7. **Losses and donations.** Keep a loss ledger by origin year, the five following periods, amounts already used and statutory ordering. Apply art. 32's remaining-balance rules; do not invent an indefinite carryforward or automatically deduct an expired amount. Qualifying charitable/sponsorship donations have the 5%-of-taxable-income limit and eligible-recipient/document requirements; statutory food-donation treatment is separate. The ordinary cash-donation cap is reconciled to approved VEN12 row 040 below; noncash/food and other special cases require their own applicable method. [Arts. 32, 36][code].
8. **Compute the SME base separately.** Use financial-accounting income for the SME period. Subtract current returns/discounts in the period they occur, including returns of prior-period sales. Exclude art. 20 income and income from exchange-rate or sum differences. Do not deduct ordinary operating expenses or use the ordinary 12% profit-base calculation. Apply 4%. Keep the short periods on entering/leaving VAT registration separate. [Arts. 54^1/1–54^4][code].
9. **Settle the actual liability.** For ordinary profit tax, apply the legal rate to the positive reconciled taxable income after eligible losses. Match qualifying foreign-tax credit to the same taxed foreign income and period, capped at Moldova's tax on that income. Credit evidenced instalments and applicable advance payments, avoiding double credit. The dividend-linked payment deferral below changes payment timing; it does not make all retained profit exempt. [Arts. 15–16, 32, 81–84, 87][code].

rows.old_text: Article 24 also has specific stock-loss, environmental, infrastructure-transfer, audit/sector, stipend and liquidation rules. Their full special procedures are not certified by this draft. The ordinary Government procedures below resolve the identified representation, business-insurance, transport/food, development and donation-documentation gaps; the travel/asset procedures below are sourced; remaining annex applications, capped-base and actual-return implementation gaps stay explicit. Do not classify a payment from a vendor name or an assumed expense percentage.

rows.old_text: ### Company disposals and the individual capital-gain boundary
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For an ordinary resident company, recognise the business disposal income and the admissible tax cost under the applicable company rules. **Do not remove half of a company’s share-disposal gain under art. 40(7).** Article 37 limits that capital-gains chapter to resident/nonresident **individuals who do not carry on business**; article 18(e)'s reference to art. 40(7) does not expand that taxpayer scope. The company's ordinary worldwide business-income and deduction rules remain arts. 14(1)(a), 18(a)/(o) and 24; depreciable property follows its separate tax-undepreciated-value method below. [Code arts. 14, 18, 24, 37–40][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Keep the nonresident rules distinct as well. Article 71(1)(c) refers to art. 40(7) for the specified nonbusiness **individual** gains; article 71(1)(d) expressly refers to art. 40(1)–(4), excluding paragraph (7), for a nonresident **legal entity** disposing of the specified Moldovan assets. Determine source, tax basis, withholding and any treaty entitlement under the cross-border method; neither route creates a universal 50% company exclusion. [Code arts. 37, 40, 71(1)(c)–(d), 91][code]; [cross-border Guide](md-cross-border.md).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Apply the ordinary deduction procedures
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Government Decision 693/2018 annex 1 supplies the operating rules below. Its latest displayed 2026 version is effective 18 June. The January/current comparison and the actual amending Decision 321/2026 show that the June changes to this business annex concern points 30 and 31; the January transport, meal and representation caps below are also retained directly. The Code prevails where a general regulatory statement is narrower or broader than the statute. [Regulation 693, annex 1][corpreg]; [January regulation][corpregjan]; [Decision 321/2026 point 2.1][corpregamend].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For an ordinary expense, record the business purpose, period, actual supplier/payee, source document, accounting treatment and any specific cap. Points 24–30 require the business connection and correct period, and permit only the business portion of mixed expenditure where business use predominates, above 50%. Recovered costs/losses/bad debts previously deducted enter gross income in the recovery year; costs never deducted use the statutory exclusion. **Do not read point 30 as overriding the specific Code art. 20(z^17) exception for provisions created in 2023–2026 when art. 87(1^1) was applied.** [Regulation points 24–30][corpreg]; [Code arts. 20(z^17), 24 and 44][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The membership/qualifying union alternatives in Code art. 24(15),(15^1) already applied from **1 January 2026** under Law 318/2025. The January regulation's union point 31 mentioned only 0.15% of payroll; June's regulatory update adds the alternative of up to two forecast monthly average salaries. Follow the January Code rather than incorrectly starting that statutory alternative in June, or adding both limits together. Keep the eligible organisation, actual dues/allocation and collective-agreement purpose distinct. For the two-salary alternative, the verified 17,400 forecast input gives **34,800**. [January Code art. 24(15),(15^1) and commencement annotations][jan]; [Regulation point 31][corpreg]; [Decision 321/2026 point 2.1.2][corpregamend]; [forecast input][average].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text:
| Ordinary expense | Limit and method | Evidence and boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Organised work/dual-education transport | 75 excluding VAT per person for each actual working/transport day; reconcile monthly cost against actual transported persons and days | Internal policy/order, person's consent, route/person lists and attendance/day-worker register/dual-training contract. Third-party/public transport needs the stated service-contract/route/distance evidence. Do not apply this commute/education limit to every other business journey. [Points 34–37][corpreg] |
| Organised employee meals | 70 excluding VAT per person per actual workday. The ordinary employer's monthly average gross pay must be at least ¾ of forecast monthly average pay, **13,050 for 2026**. Compute the employer average from monthly payroll divided by average headcount, rather than treating each individual's wage as the same test | Internal policy/order and recipient list, consent, own-food cost evidence or catering contract, and attendance. The qualifying agriculture exception uses at least 70% of the stated CAEM 01.1–01.6 activities and an average-gross-pay threshold of 9,000; it took effect 1 January 2026. Points 38/40/41 also address day workers and dual/trainee categories under their own statutory routes. [Points 38–41, including 39^1][corpreg]; [January point 39^1 annotation][corpregjan] |
| Representation/delegations received | Combined deductible representation limit **0.75% of statutory gross income**. Gifts/souvenirs have their separate **2% of annual personal-exemption amount per received person/programme** sublimit; with the 2026 standard amount 29,700 this is **594** | Business-related official receptions, specified cultural events, transport, outside translators, refreshments and qualifying gifts. Keep **both** the visit order/programme with delegation composition, purpose and dates, and the documented results/expense report. This is not the employee's separate gift/voucher allowance. [Points 51–53][corpreg]; [Code art. 33(1)][code] |
| Business insurance | Classify the actual paid premium under point 55. The combined ceiling for the listed voluntary classes **55(2)(h)–(l) is 3% of gross income from all sources**, under that provision; it is not 3% separately for every policy or a cap on every insurance class | Retain policy, insured interest/property/risk, business purpose, premium and payment evidence. State-subsidised insurance deducts only the insured's required premium share. Employee voluntary medical insurance follows its separate Code cap and benefit analysis. [Point 55][corpreg]; [Code art. 24(20)][code] |

rows.old_text: For transport/meals above the relevant cap, the regulation specifies different payroll consequences: employees have income tax, social contributions and medical premiums; day workers the stated income tax/social route; trainees/dual pupils the stated income tax/medical route. Identify the actual status and applicable base rather than applying one employee package to everybody. The taxed-payment deduction in Code art. 24(19^2)/regulation point 33^1 must be tested separately; an above-cap taxable benefit is not automatically a permanent company-tax disallowance. Use the connected payroll/social Guides for their actual rates and remaining procedures. [Regulation points 33^1, 35, 40^1][corpreg]; [Code art. 24(19^2)][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: **Representation limits apply together.** Identify eligible costs and each gift sublimit before comparing the resulting total with the overall 0.75% ceiling. Do not add a sublimit excess twice to the same overall disallowance. Establish statutory gross income under the Code; accounting sales alone are not automatically the entire cap base. The worked source controls retain their own explicit assumptions, rather than certifying a taxpayer's delegation or income classification. [Code arts. 18, 20, 24(3), 33][code]; [Regulation points 51–53][corpreg].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Point 55 covers specified compulsory motor/carrier liability and other legally compulsory business insurance, and enumerates voluntary accident, employee life/annuity, vehicle/rail/air/ship, transit-goods, property/fire/calamity, specified liability/convention and other ordinary necessary business classes. For the property/fire categories, apply the stated ownership and covered-risk conditions; do not relabel a capped class as an uncapped catch-all. Company deductibility of an employee's insurance premium does not by itself establish the employee's tax exemption. [Regulation point 55][corpreg]; [Code arts. 19–20, 24][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Employee development, recreation and required records
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Business-specific professional education under point 45 must be needed for the employee's actual role/activity and incurred exclusively for business. This differs from other development/team-building under point 45^1 and Code art. 24(19^3)(b), whose **5%** base is the selected previous/current year's payroll less the specified management-group 112/121 payroll. The Code's complete base restriction controls; the regulation's general definition of payroll as salary, other work rewards and material aid does not restore excluded management amounts. Keep internal recipient/training and activity orders, contract, invoice and supporting cost records under point 46. Do not charge the same activity to both an uncapped role-required training route and the capped recreation/development route. [Regulation points 45–46][corpreg]; [Code art. 24(19),(19^3)(b)][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For rural-tourism reimbursement/vacation vouchers, points 44^1–44^13 require the qualifying Moldovan rural facility/authorised operator and the relevant Code cap. Accrual taxpayers need the tax invoice; cash-method taxpayers additionally need evidence of actual payment. Aggregate multiple vouchers, reimbursements and the connected sports costs within the Code's shared **50%-of-forecast-average-salary per-employee annual cap**, rather than creating separate allowances for each purchase. The current 2026 input gives **8,700**. Above-cap amounts enter the stated taxable-benefit/taxed-deduction route. [Regulation points 44^1–44^7][corpreg]; [Code art. 24(19^3)(c)][code]; [forecast input][average].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The paper voucher must show the rural facility's name/IDNO, nominal value, issue date and validity period. Employer purchase/award can cover both main and concurrent jobs under the stated rule; unused-value handling follows the operator/employer contract. A value returned by the operator after expiry enters the employer's gross income in the receipt period. The employer cannot replace a voucher returned by the employee with cash compensation. Authorisation of the actual operator/facility requires the Ministry of Culture list mentioned in point 44^7; this Guide does not certify any particular provider. [Regulation points 44^7–44^13][corpreg].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Meal vouchers are a different statutory scheme under Law 166/2017, not the organised-food 70-per-day rule or rural-vacation voucher. Points 42–44 refer to that law's actual nominal limit and the taxed-excess deduction route. The current nominal meal-voucher amount and scheme implementation remain an explicit gap; do not substitute an invented figure. [Regulation points 42–44][corpreg]; [Code art. 24(19^1),(19^2)][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Donation documentation, values and losses
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For an ordinary philanthropic/sponsorship deduction, verify the Code art. 36(2) eligible recipient and statutory purpose, obtain the written beneficiary request and donation/sponsorship contract, and retain the actual transfer/payment evidence. Regulation points 58–66 permit monetary and nonmonetary forms but do not remove the **5%-of-taxable-income** ceiling or recipient/purpose requirements. For cash, the contract plus payment document is required. Noncash documentation includes a contract specifying the assets/purpose, notarisation for immovable property, the relevant recipient authorisation and the prescribed tax-invoice evidence. [Code art. 36][code]; [Regulation points 58–66][corpreg].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: A business gift of property has a **deemed-disposal income adjustment as well as any donation deduction**. Code art. 21(5) uses the greater of tax-undepreciated value and market value, with its explicit qualifying food-donation exception under Law 299/2022. Regulation point 64 addresses the residual-value/market comparison and nondepreciable-property book/market rule. Reconcile disposal proceeds, tax basis and the eligible donation separately; do not simply deduct the accounting expense and ignore deemed income. The food-donation exception and precise capped-base/return-line calculation need their own applicable procedure; no result for those open computations is certified here. [Code arts. 21(5), 36][code]; [Regulation points 64–66][corpreg].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Maintain loss-origin years and the version that governed each origin. Regulation points 76–78 support a tax loss based on allowed deductions exceeding gross income and require the origin-period art. 32 rules, with the legacy 2017–2022 table. Use current Code art. 32 for the applicable five-period/ordering method. The approved return and any particular historic-origin exception still require reconciliation; an old table's “unlimited” entry does not establish unlimited carryforward years. [Regulation points 76–78][corpreg]; [Code art. 32][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Foreign currency and connected-party values
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For ordinary income tax, Code art. 21(3) converts foreign-currency receipts/income/expenses at the official MDL rate for the transaction date. Its date rule uses the bank/payment-company statement or, in other cases, primary documents under the applicable SNC/IFRS accounting method; do not automatically use a single invoice/payment-date shortcut for every accrual. At fiscal year-end, retranslate foreign-currency debts due by/to the taxpayer at the final-day official rate, **excluding advances for assets/services**. Recognise the stipulated current/year-end exchange differences under the Code's period rules. For a currency not quoted by BNM, the provision prescribes conversion through a BNM-quoted currency using the direct relationship, then into MDL. Retain the actual rate, date, method and source evidence. [Code art. 21(3), points 1–4 including 2^1 and 3^1–3^3][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The SME base's specific FX/sum-difference exclusion remains separate; do not move ordinary-company exchange treatment into the 4% base. For below-market business dealings with nonbusiness individual founders/other related individuals, art. 21(6) requires its market adjustment, with the stated arm's-length/art. 19 exceptions. For an unlisted/self-created asset or component, the internal commission, independent expert or manufacturer/supplier/distributor recommendation establishes the life with subsequent management approval. rows.old_text: Ordinary straight-line depreciation starts in the **month after commissioning**, and capitalised subsequent costs start in the month after capitalisation. The final depreciation month includes expiry, withdrawal from service or disposal. Compute `depreciable value × (1 / useful life in years) × eligible months / 12`; equivalently use a life in months consistently. Reconcile the last-period total with the available basis. The regulation also prorates months when a business first becomes entitled to deductions on moving from a special regime; it has particular adjusted-basis rules for that change and withdrawal of IT-park residence. Finance/operating leases and IFRS right-of-use assets follow their distinct statutory owner/deduction rules. [Code art. 26^1(4)–(7)][code]; [regulation points 2, 10–19][assetreg].

That first year is **12 consecutive months of useful life**, not automatically the calendar year of purchase. Record the election, actual qualifying months, tax depreciation already taken and remaining life; do not take a full first-year amount twice across two calendar returns. [Code art. 26^1(6^1)][code]; [regulation point 16^4, amendment effective 1 January 2025][assetreg].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Separate servicing/maintenance from repair and capital improvement. SNC/IFRS current expenses follow Code art. 24(1); capitalised improvements increase entry cost and depreciation uses the adjusted undepreciated basis over the remaining life from the next month. Life extensions/reductions follow catalogue points 10–11, including the minimum-life safeguard. For qualifying rented/leased/concession assets whose repairs are borne by the user, the Code normally caps current deduction at **15% of accrued annual rent/operating-lease/concession charges**; the specified international-aircraft route uses 100% of operating-lease charges, and own taxi-vehicle repairs have their separate 100% rule. Regulation point 28 permits full current deduction of the specified leased/rented/other-use-contract repairs where the contract lasts **up to 12 months inclusive**. Do not apply a universal 15% cap to owned-asset maintenance. [Code arts. 24(1), 26^1(3), (11)–(11^1)][code]; [regulation points 20–28][assetreg]; [catalogue points 10–11][assetcatalogue].

rows.old_text: An applicable repair excess becomes a separately registered tax asset when the work is complete. Its starting life is the shorter of remaining contract term and the underlying asset's useful life; the entity can elect a longer life. Multiple repairs can be one investment asset or separate ones under point 29. If the contract is terminated, point 30 retains the investment in the register and continues depreciation over its originally fixed duration. Obtain the actual contract, repair allocation and completion records before deciding the route. [Points 24–30][assetreg].

rows.old_text: On disposal, determine tax undepreciated value from entry/capitalised cost less tax depreciation **through the disposal month**. A sale's tax result is proceeds less that value. A donation produces the positive excess of market value over tax undepreciated value, or zero where the latter is higher, subject to the Code's specific controlling exceptions. An exchange uses the received asset's contractual value adjusted for extra cash receivable/payable, less the transferred asset's tax undepreciated value. A capital contribution uses the participation interest's value less the transferred asset's tax undepreciated value. **Forced loss or early scrapping does not automatically deduct the remaining tax value**: where qualifying insurance/co-insurance compensation is taxable under Code art. 18(i), point 36 permits deduction only up to that taxable income. Historical capped-car and transition assets have separate points 33^1, 35^1 and 38–45; keep their original-period schedules instead of resetting their tax basis to book value. [Code arts. 18(i), 21(5), 26^1(17)][code]; [regulation points 31–45][assetreg].

rows.old_text: ## Two worked examples that recompute
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### 1. Ordinary company reconciliation, loss and foreign credit
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Assume a resident ordinary company outside the special/deferral regimes. Accounting revenue is 1,000,000 and accounting expenses 700,000, including a nondeductible statutory fine of 5,000 and book depreciation 50,000. The separately verified asset schedule supports tax depreciation 40,000; this example does not determine asset lives. An unexpired earliest loss of 100,000 is fully usable under the origin-year schedule. The reconciled profit includes 50,000 of net foreign income taxable in Moldova at 12%, with certified qualifying foreign tax 8,000. No other adjustments/credits; evidenced instalments are 18,000. Taxable income is 215,000, tax 25,800, allowable foreign credit 6,000 and final balance 1,800. [Arts. 15, 26^1, 30, 32, 44, 82–87][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text:
```oa-check
name: Moldova 2026 ordinary corporate loss and capped foreign credit
inputs:
  accounting_revenue: 1000000
  accounting_expenses: 700000
  statutory_fine: 5000
  book_depreciation: 50000
  verified_tax_depreciation: 40000
  eligible_unexpired_loss: 100000
  same_foreign_net_income: 50000
  certified_foreign_tax: 8000
  evidenced_instalments: 18000
steps:
  accounting_profit: accounting_revenue - accounting_expenses
  profit_before_losses: accounting_profit + statutory_fine + book_depreciation - verified_tax_depreciation
  taxable_income: max(0, profit_before_losses - eligible_unexpired_loss)
  gross_tax: taxable_income * 0.12
  foreign_tax_cap: same_foreign_net_income * 0.12
  allowed_foreign_credit: min(certified_foreign_tax, foreign_tax_cap)
  final_tax: max(0, gross_tax - allowed_foreign_credit)
  balance_due: final_tax - evidenced_instalments
expected:
  accounting_profit: 300000
  profit_before_losses: 315000
  taxable_income: 215000
  gross_tax: 25800
  foreign_tax_cap: 6000
  allowed_foreign_credit: 6000
  final_tax: 19800
  balance_due: 1800
```

rows.old_text: ### 2. Eligible SME accounting-income base

rows.old_text: Assume the taxpayer has established eligibility, a timely 2026 SME election, no VAT registration/change and no prohibited consultancy/shareholding facts. These exclusions do not overlap; no return has already been deducted. Ordinary operating expenses do not reduce this base. The resulting 920,000 base gives 36,800 tax at 4%; evidenced quarterly payments of 30,000 leave 6,800. [Arts. 54^1–54^4][code].

- What is the legal/taxpayer category, residence, tax period, VAT registration history and elected tax regime? Supply the actual accounting policy and prior-year income/classification tests.

rows.old_text: Determine **the person, residence, income category, source, PE connection and payer** before choosing a rate. Use the Fiscal Code consolidated through the amendment effective 30 October 2026; selected operative articles were read, not every provision of the Code. rows.old_text: ### Residence and the taxable population
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: An individual is domestically resident if either they have a permanent domicile in Moldova or they spend **at least 183 days during the fiscal year** in Moldova. The domicile limb includes specified absences for treatment, holidays, study or business travel and Moldovan officials exercising functions abroad. Article 5(6) gives nonresident exceptions for diplomatic/consular personnel and families, specified treaty-created international-organisation staff and families, persons present exclusively for treatment, holidays or study, and transit. A company or organisational form is resident where its activity is organised or managed in Moldova or its main place of activity is Moldova. Incorporation abroad does not by itself settle the domestic residence of a business managed in Moldova. Domestic residence does not decide a dual-residence treaty claim; establish the actual treaty and its operative residence article separately. [Code art. 5(5)–(6)](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro).

rows.old_text: ## Penalties and interest
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: **Calendar-2026 ordinary tax late charge.** Code art. 228(3) and the BNM decision of 6 November 2025, point 1, supply the calculation: the retained **6.00%** short-term policy rate, rounded up to a whole percent, plus **5 percentage points**, divided by **365 days**, gives **0.0301% per delayed day** after rounding the daily percentage to four decimal places. The decimal multiplier is **0.000301**. Apply it to the established outstanding principal for each chargeable day; split changes in principal and calendar year. This calculation concerns debts governed by art. 228 and does not replace a separate statutory regime's rate or establish case-specific relief. [Code art. 228(2)–(3)](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro); [BNM decision, point 1](https://bnm.md/en/node/69226).

A residence document or adviser instruction does not transfer that statutory responsibility. [Code art. 79³(8)](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro).

Establish the actual offence and responsible population before quoting a sanction. Article 261(4) provides **20%–30% of understated tax** for understatement through a return with untrue data; art. 261(4¹) has the stated truthful self-correction exception under art. 188. Article 261(5) separately provides **80%–100%** for the described evasion of calculation/payment of undeclared percentage-based liabilities. These are different offences, not three automatic additions to every missed withholding payment. [Code arts. 232, 260(1), 261(4)–(5), 188](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro).

Use the verified calendar-2026 calculation above for debts governed by art. 228, with the actual statutory exceptions. Article 228(2¹) limits interest to the corresponding liability for the stated corrected/erroneous-calculation cases; art. 228(5)–(7) contains documented transfer/offset, budget-funded receivable, special-accounting and bank-timing exceptions. Article 79³(1) provides the more favourable rate where domestic and treaty rates differ and directs use of OECD Model Commentaries for interpretation. This does not create a single universal treaty rate, residence tie-breaker or employment exemption. Retrieve the actual agreement, subsequent protocols, operative dates and any applicable multilateral modifications; determine residence, income article, PE attribution, beneficial-owner and anti-abuse conditions from those texts. rows.old_text:
- A nonresident **individual** supplies the competent residence-state authority's residence certificate, in original paper and/or electronic form, **before income payment**.
- A nonresident **legal person** supplies a copy of the residence certificate, or a document proving registration in the residence country, or an extract from that state's official authority website confirming fiscal residence or registration. This domestic documentary alternative does not itself establish substantive treaty entitlement.

A certificate issued for a fiscal period also applies during the first **60 days** of the next period unless those conditions change. The payer recalculates at treaty rates and files a corrected tax report with its SFS subdivision. Article 79³(3) separately provides refund to the payer or nonresident on the nonresident's request within the statutory limitation period. The exact limitation computation and implementing forms/documents have not been verified here. [Code art. 79³(2¹)–(4)](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro).

rows.old_text: ## Two worked examples that recompute

rows.old_text: ### 1. Distinguish income categories before withholding
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Assume an ordinary Moldovan company pays nonresidents without a Moldovan PE, without applicable treaty relief: management consultancy **100,000** within art. 71(b), a qualifying copyright reproduction royalty **50,000**, current-profit dividends **200,000**, and dividends attributable to 2008–2011 profits **20,000**. Separately it pays **80,000** for goods under art. 71(a) and **40,000** for residual services performed wholly outside Moldova that are established not to fall within another Moldova-source category. These are hypothetical classified facts, not conclusions inferred from invoice labels.

rows.old_text: Withholding is **12,000 + 6,000 + 12,000 + 3,000 = 33,000**. Total contractual payments are **490,000** and net paid is **457,000**. The goods and the specified offshore residual services contribute zero to this particular withholding computation for different reasons; no PE, VAT/customs or other-country exemption follows. IPC21 maps royalties to 51, dividends to 54 and the consultancy to the applicable other-payment entry 56. Do not assume a payment excluded from withholding is therefore omitted from every reporting requirement. [Code arts. 71(a),(b),(b¹),(e),(j), 73, 91](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro); [IPC21 annex 2 Table 1](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=154168&lang=ro).

```oa-check
name: Moldova nonresident income categories and net payments
inputs:
  consultancy: 100000
  copyright_royalty: 50000
  current_profit_dividend: 200000

  goods: 80000

  royalty_tax: 6000

```

rows.old_text: ### 2. Cap the foreign credit at Moldova tax on that income

That foreign income is taxable in Moldova in the same period, the competent foreign authority's acceptable evidence confirms **30,000** of foreign income tax paid, and there are no other reliefs, losses or credits. The 12% regime and all bases are stipulated; this is not a turnover-tax or IT-park example.

The **6,000** foreign-tax excess is not treated as a Moldova refund/carryforward or a credit against domestic income. This computation does not decide a timing mismatch, mixed tax base, multiple-stream allocation or foreign treaty-refund claim. rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ## Who this applies to
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Use this overview to identify the taxpayer, period, tax base and connected Moldova Guide before calculating an ordinary 2026 liability. Headline rates are not a complete tax computation or proof of eligibility for a special regime. The pack remains a source-cited draft with stated gaps and a bounded source-review record linked under Sources. [Code arts. 12^1–15, 83, 96, 114–115][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The **Serviciul Fiscal de Stat (SFS)** administers taxes and other covered public payments. The national currency is the **Moldovan leu**; examples below show MDL amounts. Accounting and tax-conversion rules still depend on the transaction and applicable provision. [Code art. 129(2)][code]; [BNM national-currency section][bnm]; [Accounting Law art. 7][accounts].

rows.old_text: ## Rates, bands and thresholds
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text:
| Ordinary headline | Rate or period | Primary source |
|---|---|---|
| Individual/individual-entrepreneur and listed professional income tax | **12% of annual taxable income**, with the actual taxpayer/base/regime classification | [Code art. 15(a)][code] |
| Legal-person income tax | **12% of taxable income**, subject to actual special/exempt regimes | [Code art. 15(b)][code] |
| Standard VAT | **20%** of the taxable value; reduced rates and exemptions require their own conditions | [Code art. 96(a)–(b)][code] |
| Ordinary income-tax period | Calendar year; first-year, liquidation, reorganisation, IT-park and permitted non-calendar-period rules are separate | [Code art. 12^1][code] |
| Ordinary VAT period | Calendar month; article 94(d)'s specified electronic-services category has a quarterly period | [Code art. 114(1)–(1^1)][code] |
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: These figures do not replace the [individual](moldova-income-tax.md), [corporate](md-corporate-income-tax.md), [VAT](moldova-vat.md), [payroll](moldova-payroll.md) or [social/medical](moldova-social-contributions.md) calculations. Classification comes before applying a percentage. A business's legal form does not by itself select the small-business, independent-service, IT-park or other special regime. [Code arts. 13–15, 83, 96][code].

rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

Establish the actual facts and any treaty instead of applying an individual day count to every entity. The income-object populations below are a separate question. [Code art. 5(5)][code]; [individual](moldova-income-tax.md) / [cross-border](md-cross-border.md).

rows.old_text: ## The base
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Do not apply a blanket “every resident is taxed on all worldwide income” rule. Articles 13–14 distinguish:
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text:
- Resident businesses, listed professional/service activities and legal persons, whose covered business object includes domestic and foreign sources, subject to the actual deductions/exemptions.
- Resident Moldovan citizens outside business, whose domestic/work-in-Moldova object and foreign investment/financial income are addressed separately.
- Resident foreign citizens and stateless individuals working in Moldova, whose listed work/source object excludes foreign investment/financial income under the cited paragraph.
- Nonresident individuals outside Moldovan business, whose covered Moldova-source income follows chapter 11; entities, permanent establishments, payer withholding and treaties require the [cross-border method](md-cross-border.md).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Those distinctions are statutory populations, not proof that an individual is resident or that a receipt is exempt. Establish legal residence, citizenship where relevant, actual activity, source, income type, permanent establishment, timing and special/final-withholding regime. [Code arts. 13–14][code]; [cross-border Guide](md-cross-border.md).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For income tax, determine taxable income after the deductions/exemptions legally available to the taxpayer. Do not tax all cash received as profit, deduct an employer's social expense from employee cash, or treat loan principal as salary. For VAT, classify the transaction and tax point, rate/exemption and legally deductible input; output VAT is not automatically the amount payable. Use the connected Guides' retained rules and unresolved limits. [Code arts. 12(4), (11)–(13), 14–15, 19, 101–102][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

| Qualifying non-VAT individual entrepreneur/peasant farm | Specified unified report by **25 March**, with annual average employees not exceeding **five** and all statutory conditions | [Code art. 83(11)][code] |
| Income-tax payment | Ordinarily by the statutory return deadline; a filing extension does not automatically extend payment | [Code art. 87(1)][code] |

For tax deadlines, article 129(8) supplies the stated non-working-day rollover and electronic end-of-day rule; it does not settle every separate company-law deadline. Retain the current form, submitted version, acceptance receipt, liability period and actual payment allocation. [Code arts. 12^1, 129(8)][code].

rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.
