This is a reporting map, not evidence that every listed tax applies or that a single national rate can be used. Obtain the current taxing law, local decision where required, taxable object, period, cadastral/accounting evidence and any specific relief before entering an amount. The separate [individual-income method](moldova-income-tax.md) establishes the UNIF25 taxpayer and reporting year. [SFS Order 300/2025](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=148910&lang=ro); [actual form](https://www.legis.md/UserFiles/Image/RO/2025/mo309-312ro/an1_300ro.docx), [instructions 121–136](https://www.legis.md/UserFiles/Image/RO/2025/mo309-312ro/an2_300ro.docx).

rows.old_text: ## Penalties and interest
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Use the actual tax, principal, due date, payment/change dates and statutory exception. The connected tax Guides supply the ordinary 2026 tax/medical late-charge calculation and separate social charge with their sources. rows.old_text: ## Two worked examples that recompute
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### 1. Ordinary company with an established taxable base
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Assume an ordinary resident company has 100,000 MDL of taxable income after all established adjustments, no exemption/special regime, no foreign credit and no advance payments. The 12% charge is 12,000 MDL. This is a computation on the assumed taxable base, not a conclusion that turnover or bank receipts equal profit. [Code arts. 12(4), 14(1)(a), 15(b)][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

name: Moldova 2026 overview ordinary corporate income-tax charge
inputs:
  established_taxable_income: 100000
  ordinary_rate: 0.12
steps:

expected:
  income_tax: 12000
```
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### 2. Ordinary standard-rated VAT with established deductible input
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Assume an ordinary registered taxpayer has 100,000 MDL of standard-rated domestic taxable value in the month and 8,000 MDL of legally deductible input VAT in that period. There are no exemptions, mixed-use/prorata issues, earlier balances or other adjustments. Output VAT is 20,000 MDL and the current net amount is 12,000 MDL. The assumed input entitlement must be established under the actual conditions before using the subtraction. [Code arts. 96(a), 101(1), 102][code].

rows.old_text: # Moldova transfer pricing v0.8
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: 2026 draft, primary law read 30 October 2026; the current information annex and APA application model read 31 October 2026. The 24 October draft and its independent correction evidence are preserved; that review does not attest to this expanded country pack. This Guide provides the domestic TP computation/documentation method. Actual comparables, legal facts and any treaty relief must be evidenced before use.
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ## Who this applies to
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Start with the current Fiscal Code TitleV chapter 11², arts. 226¹⁷–226³⁰, and Ministry of Finance Order 9/2024 as amended, including Order 8/2026. The rules apply to Moldovan-registered business legal/natural persons and foreign legal persons with Moldovan branches/permanent establishments. Art. 226¹⁹(9) excludes Moldovan-citizen individuals not carrying on business from that article's filing rule. The arm's-length obligation is separate from the information/file threshold. [Code arts. 226¹⁷–226¹⁹](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro), [Order 9 annex 1 points 1–2](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152738&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Under 226¹⁷(1)(1), affiliation includes spouses or relatives up to the second degree; an individual/legal-person relationship with at least 25% direct/indirect voting participation including affiliated holdings or effective control; a legal-person/legal-person relationship on the same basis; and common third-person ownership/control of both. Effective control includes the specified majority board/executive/auditor appointment/removal powers and contractual/constitutional/agreed control. Indirect participation can pass through several people/entities; the legal person and its PE are affiliated. Do not stop the test at a 25% share register where another control limb applies. [Code 226¹⁷](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: A transaction includes sales, purchases, giving/receiving services, assignments, leases, credit, loans and transfers of interests or rights in tangible/intangible property. A local transaction under 226¹⁷(1)(9) concerns residents where either/both have the specified free-zone/IT-park status or different business-income tax rates/bases; a cross-border transaction under(10) is between a resident and a nonresident outside Moldova. Classify the parties, regimes and transaction before applying 226¹⁸(2). Do not treat every same-rate domestic intercompany movement as automatically satisfying the statutory local-transaction definition, or omit eligible domestic transactions solely because neither party is foreign. [Code 226¹⁷–226¹⁸](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The current 226¹⁹ filing structure applies from fiscal period 2025 under Law 187/2025 art. XXVI(1)(b). It replaced the two-tier 20m/50m system: for 2025/2026 periods there is one information threshold and a request-based file. For 2024, Law 187 art. XXVI(3) creates a separate request/120-day file transition for its specified former category and disapplies the identified non-submission sanction for the former deadline; do not apply an old automatic filing calendar or treat that transition as the 2026 rule. [Law 187 art. II point 19 and art. XXVI](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=149593&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The 20m filing threshold is not a safe-harbour price, deductible-expense limit or separate TP tax rate. Regulated/judicially set price elements fall within the deemed arm's-length rule in 226¹⁸(3); retain the instrument and demonstrate that it governs the actual element. Income/expense adjustments operate through Titles II/X and **do not alter VAT** on supplies/purchases under 226¹⁸(4),(6). [Code](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ## The base
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Build the affiliate and threshold reconciliation
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Identify ownership/control and fiscal periods; record each party's residence, PE and tax regime. Reconcile transaction values across all eligible affiliates **without VAT**, maintaining sales and purchases separately instead of netting bilateral balances. Tag legal exclusions individually. Art. 226¹⁹(4) excludes transactions covered by an actual APA from the threshold and its documentation, whereas a pending APA application does not exempt the information filing under Order 9 annex 3 point 4. [Code 226¹⁹](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro), [Order 9](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152738&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Art. 226¹⁹(7) excludes received/paid advances, exchange differences and accounting revaluation differences of assets/liabilities arising from affiliated transactions, except actual currency-exchange transactions. For leases, credit and loans, the threshold includes **only interest calculated during the fiscal period** under art. 12(7), rather than the funding principal or all instalments. Preserve the bridge from accounting/contract data to eligible amounts; do not use the expired Order 9 point 52 as if it overrode current statutory exclusions. Foreign-currency conversion mechanics and unusual financing components require the confirmed rule stated below before using an assumed exchange rate. [Code 226¹⁹(7)](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro), [current Order 9 annex 1 point 52 repealed](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152738&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Below 20m, the statutory information/request-file obligation under 226¹⁹(1) is not triggered solely by value; it does not prove arm's-length pricing or remove ordinary evidence duties. Order 9 annex 1 point 36 permits SFS to require structure/affiliation, markets, competitors, contracts, accounting and transaction-support records from persons without the file obligation; point 37 says missing documents do not stop the audit. The old point 30 MDL 1m verification exclusion is repealed in the current rules. [Code 226¹⁸–226²⁰](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro), [Order 9 annex 1 points 30–37](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152738&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Delineate and price the actual transaction
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The taxpayer bears the burden of demonstrating arm's-length compliance. Compare legal, economic, commercial and financial conditions using characteristics, functions/assets/risks, contractual terms, economic circumstances and business strategy. Record risk control and financial capacity, not only a contract allocating the risk. The actual conduct/conditions prevail where inconsistent with the document. Examine markets, competition, substitutes, supply/demand, purchasing power, regulation and infrastructure; justify a different geographic market and reliable adjustments. [Code 226¹⁸(7)–(8),226²⁰(5)](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro), [Order 9 annex 1 points 4–13](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152738&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Select the most appropriate method and document why the data and comparability support it. The domestic methods are comparable uncontrolled price (CUP), cost-plus, resale-price, transactional net margin (TNMM), profit-split, and another method recognised in the OECD TP Guidelines. Do not invent a universal statutory cost-plus markup, guarantee fee or interest margin. [Code 226²⁰(3)–(5)](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text:
| Method | Computation and evidence to retain | Official provision |
|---|---|---|
|CUP|Compare actual controlled unit price with sufficiently comparable independent prices, adjusting material differences reliably|Order 9 annex 1 point 16|
|Resale price|Independent resale price less the justified resale margin (resale costs and appropriate gross profit), adjusting relevant acquisition costs; keep consistent gross-margin accounting|Point 17|
|Cost-plus|Relevant production/service costs plus a justified gross-profit markup; retain cost-pool, allocation and functions/risks/asset analysis|Point 18|
|TNMM|Compare a properly delineated tested party's relevant net-profit indicator with reliable independent/internal uncontrolled results; reconcile the chosen denominator and segment accounts|Point 19 and 21|
|Profit-split|Delineate the relevant combined profit and allocate consistently with evidenced contributions/functions/risks/assets and independent conditions|Point 20|
|Other OECD-recognised method|Explain its suitability to the actual case and data under the statutory most-appropriate-method criteria|Code 226²⁰(3)(f),(5)|
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Table sources: [Order 9 annex 1 points 14–21](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152738&lang=ro), [Code 226²⁰](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro). Resale, cost-plus and TNMM require a tested-party selection under point 21. A group policy or a database printout without delineation, comparable selection, adjustments and accounting reconciliation is not the required conclusion.
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Build the comparability interval from the justified independent data. Points 22–24 use the lower/upper quartiles as the interval bounds. Point 25's special rule for at most two comparable values uses the minimum/maximum and arithmetic mean for the median. Preserve the data, rejection log, search date, formula and adjustments; the actual quartile interpolation algorithm for larger samples is not prescribed here and remains a precise gap below. A result within a properly established interval is treated as arm's-length; audit adjustment/estimation uses the median under 47. [Order 9 annex 1 points 3,22–25,47](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152738&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Voluntary and corresponding adjustments
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Art. 226²³ allows voluntary income/expense adjustment; for prior periods submit the required corrected information/file and corrected tax returns under 188. Order 9 annex 1 points 26–28 permits adjustment within the interval where pricing is not arm's-length but prevents voluntary correction of the controlled transactions once a TP audit of one of the relevant affiliates has started. SFS can adjust where the principle fails, or estimate where necessary data are absent, and can use another method after demonstrating failure of the taxpayer's method. The amended rules use a thematic tax audit; the former preliminary-review procedure and its protection in repealed point 44 must not be reused as a current amnesty. [Code 226²⁰,226²³,188](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro), [Order 9 annex 1 points 26–49](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152738&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For resident affiliates, 226²¹ makes the SFS adjustment/estimation opposable to the other party. SFS issues the counterpart decision after the 226²¹/252(3) stage, and the other party can amend its income-tax return; where 188(4) blocks amendment, request an audit for double-tax elimination. Order 9 annex 1 point 55(1) specifies 15 working days after the 252(3) 30-day period; its other limb still references the now-repealed point 43, so do not invent a surviving notification process for that branch. For foreign-affiliate adjustments, follow the treaty-dependent application and evidence in Cross-border points below. [Code 226²¹–226²²,252](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro), [Order 9 annex 1 points 54–56](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152738&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Compile the master file and local file
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For periods from 2025, Order 8/2026 points 2–4 and current Order 9 annex 1 point 50 prescribe:
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text:
- **Master file:** legal/ownership structure and geography; business drivers/value chain, significant intragroup services, markets, group functions/risks/assets and restructuring; intangible strategy, ownership, agreements, DEMPE and transfers; intragroup/independent financing policy and treasury entities; consolidated financial information or the stated equivalent/segment data; APAs and relevant allocation rulings. DEMPE means development, enhancement, maintenance, protection and exploitation, not legal ownership alone.
- **Local file:** local structure, all affiliates/PEs and direct/indirect affiliation; business/markets/pricing and competitors; each controlled transaction's property/service characteristics and contracts/context, restructuring, service cost allocations and cost-contribution arrangements; detailed functional/comparability analysis; method and tested-party selection; internal/external comparables, search method/data; interval, adjustments and the reasoned arm's-length conclusion.
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Use the whole-group master information. Point 51 permits the relevant group segment if complete information is unavailable **and justified reasons are supplied**; this is not an unconditional master-file waiver. The local file must be Romanian; the master file can be Romanian, Russian or English. Paper and/or electronic files are permitted; electronic local/master files require the specified responsible resident taxpayer signatures, with identification of the master-file preparer. Requested copies of underlying contracts/documents require authorised Romanian translation except English/Russian. The information filing itself carries the responsible electronic signature. [Order 9 annex 1 points 50–53²](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152738&lang=ro), [Order 8](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152708&lang=ro).

The current retention rule is expressly unconfirmed below. Preserve the records pending resolution; do not destroy them on an assumed expiry.

rows.old_text: ## Deadlines and filing
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Reconcile a voluntary income/expense adjustment with the income-tax return as well as the TP information/file. The [corporate Guide](md-corporate-income-tax.md) identifies the VEN12 adjustment rows verified directly from enacted MF Order 145/2024. Those return rows are separate from the Order 9 annex-2 information form, whose current fields and code mappings are supplied below. [MF Order 145/2024, read 30 October 2026](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=146071&lang=ro); [Code art. 226²³](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Use the actual tax period, including a legally adopted non-calendar fiscal period under art. 12¹, rather than the parent group's reporting calendar by default. The information deadline is the 25th of month six after that period ends. Thus a calendar 2026 period has a statutory 25 June 2027 deadline before any applicable nonworking-day adjustment; a valid 30 June 2026 period has 25 December 2026 on that same basis. The taxpayer's actual fiscal-period eligibility and general calendar adjustment must be confirmed before fixing a live deadline. File-request due time is 120-days from the request but cannot fall before the information deadline; monitor the actual valid request/communication, not an informal conversation. [Code 226¹⁹(2)–(3),12¹](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Annual information is distinct from the requested file and APA application/report. Current Order 9 annex 1 points 53¹–53² requires the approved annex 2 information and responsible electronic signature. Order 8 adds fiscal-period identifiers to annexA row 5, annexB row 6 and annexC row 8, and updates annexB table 2 to sequence, transaction code, object/contract details, party-role code, controlled amount and optional comments. The complete current annex 2, including transaction-role, method, indicator and country catalogues, has now been read and retained; use its field mappings below. Authenticated electronic-field acceptance and legacy country-code handling remain untested. The 12 May 2026 SFS launch notice identifies the electronic-declaration service in the taxpayer cabinet for periods from 2025, but a portal receipt is still required for the actual filing. [Order 9](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152738&lang=ro), [Order 8 points 1.3,4](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152708&lang=ro), [SFS launch notice](https://www.sfs.md/ro/stiri/formularul-privind-preturile-de-transfer-disponibil-in-sia-declaratia-electronica).

rows.old_text: Correct information under 226¹⁹(5)/188, using the form and method valid for the corrected period, subject to 188's six-year and audit restrictions. A corrected **file** has the separate 30-day decision-communication rule in 226¹⁹(6); do not turn it into a general extension of an original request. Titles II/X determine the related return; the special IT-park TP single-tax return under 373(1¹) is not automatically an ordinary 12% corporation-tax calculation. Its actual current forms and field computation are supplied below, with the specific minimum/refund-floor and portal ambiguities retained. rows.old_text: ## Who this applies to
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Use this Guide for the refund application following a reconciled [Moldova VAT return](moldova-vat.md). First identify the actual statutory entitlement. A credit carried forward is not itself an entitlement to cash: without a refund request, HG93 point 6 carries the excess into the next period. The statutory route, supply classification, actual payment evidence and SFS decision must all match. [Fiscal Code 101(2),(8),101¹–101⁸](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro); [HG93 points 2–6](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152472&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The current Code repeals article 101⁴. HG93 still contains PPP references to that article; those references do not revive a repealed entitlement. Likewise its article 101¹ building wording predates the current Code's commissioned-and-used test. Apply the Code first. The renewable-storage route in Code 101⁸ and agricultural reimbursement programme require their own operative implementation; the gaps under Sources remain open.

rows.old_text: ## The base
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Prepare a period-by-period workpaper. Reconcile the opening credit to the previous return, eligible current input, output, adjustments, prior refunds and closing credit. Separate paid and unpaid VAT, recording the date of actual payment required by the particular route. A deductible invoice can be unpaid even when its VAT is already in the return; deduction and refund payment conditions are different. [HG93 points 26–30,35¹,38¹,47³–47⁴](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152472&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For the ordinary exemption-with-credit route, determine which deductible input VAT is paid at initiation of the audit, then allocate output first against unpaid deductible input and then paid input. The refundable amount is the smallest of the remaining overall excess, remaining paid credit and supply-based cap. The official annex 2¹ example expressly demonstrates this order. Do not calculate the paid-input ceiling before allocating output and then use that higher figure after output has consumed paid credit. [HG93 points 35¹,38¹ and annex 2¹](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152472&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For the Code 101⁶ route, first confirm that the applicant is registered as a VAT payer. Maintain separate chronological buckets: unpaid credits from January 2023 onward, paid credits from January 2023 onward, then December 2022 carry-forward. Determine eligible paid inputs at application; include the specified budget-paid VAT for cross-Nistru, insolvency and pledged/seized-property acquisitions where the conditions apply. Use the programme's own 70% ceiling and paid-excess calculation, not the export cap. Requested refunds reduce subsequent carry-forward under Code 101⁶(2). [HG93 point 47³; Code 101⁶](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152472&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Do not include national-public-budget-funded investment VAT in the investment refund. For buildings retain commissioning and actual-use evidence. An unfinished, conserved or merely purchased building does not satisfy the current commissioned-and-used condition. For a supplementary claim for a previously refunded period, apply all three HG93 point 30 tests: minimum intervening credit, no intervening VAT-payable obligation, and the applicable payment requirement. Do not refund the same input again. [Code 101¹](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro); [HG93 point 30,42¹,44](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152472&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ## Deadlines and filing
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text:
1. **Identify the law and period.** Match the route above to the actual taxpayer and supply. Reconcile each requested month to submitted VAT12 returns. The ordinary request equals the return's requested refund; HG93 point 8 contains specific exceptions for nonregistered statutory routes and agricultural-machinery-input claims. Check the current statute before using any legacy exemption.
2. **Complete the actual approved annex 1.** Enter fiscal code, legal name, registered address/street/number and telephone. Enter the requested MDL amount and exact law/article. Enter start and end month/year as `MM/YYYY`; for one month repeat the same period in both fields. An application with no requested amount is not examined. These are named fields, not numbered boxes.
3. **Give settlement instructions.** State the taxpayer's own bank/payment-account IBAN or future-obligation allocation. The table has economic-classification code, locality code, principal/fines and late charges, plus total. SFS offsets arrears first; the bank instruction concerns the confirmed amount left after that offset. Date and have the head sign the application. Do not direct the taxpayer's refund to a creditor or assignee.
4. **Assemble route-specific proof.** Provide purchase and sales registers. E-Factura invoices need not be printed. For ordinary exported goods retain export contract, commercial/tax invoice, international transport proof except the postal exception, and customs export confirmation; postal exports also need the postal document identified in the customs declaration. For exported services retain foreign-customer confirmation, payment proof/account extracts and, where linked to exported physical goods, customs and outward transport proof. Translate customer confirmation through an authorised translator when required; Russian/English confirmation is excepted from that translation requirement. Electronic services have the specific foreign-recipient/payment-identification rule. Retain investment purchase/customs/payment proof; apply the particular point 32 subparagraph for transport, leasing, zones and other supplies.
5. **Submit the signed application to SFS.** Keep the dated receipt and exact submitted version. Retain proof that the corresponding VAT12 returns were submitted; ordinary requests are examined only after those returns. The application is distinct from filing VAT12. See the official annex 1 link under Sources. Do not invent a separate portal box or treat a saved application as received.
6. **Track the authority's procedure.** Ordinary HG93 point 12 route selection is within 3 working days; its listed investment/special-scheme exceptions matter. No-prior-thematic-audit treatment requires all point 13 conditions: at least 2 years' activity, at least 2 previous refunds, no more than 12 months since the last audited refund period for large taxpayers or 24 for others, exact agreement between claimed/confirmed amount at the last thematic audit, and last-audit extra liabilities no more than 3% of supplies in the audited periods. Otherwise SFS initiates thematic audit. Later audit still occurs at least every 12/24 months. Points 12 and 13 have different printed exclusion lists; do not assume the no-audit branch for a special scheme from point 12 alone.
7. **Reconcile decision to payment.** SFS leadership decides; reasons for a partial refund/refusal must appear in the audit act. Record confirmed amount, arrears offset, future-tax allocation, bank amount and remaining credit separately. Treasury execution follows SFS's payment documents. A decision is not evidence of cash received. Challenge an adverse decision under Title V; use the underlying act's notified appeal route and clock.

rows.old_text: ## Penalties and interest
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Retain the refund decision, submitted evidence and subsequent corrections. A refusal is not automatically a tax penalty. Incorrect VAT reporting engages the assessment/late-charge rules in the [VAT return Guide](moldova-vat.md#penalties-and-interest); do not calculate a late charge on a refused refund without an actual unpaid tax debt.
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For a late authority refund, Code 176(3) provides taxpayer interest after the statutory refund period, using the previous November BNM base rate rounded up to the next whole percentage plus 5 points, divided by days in the year and rounded to 4 decimal places as a daily percentage. The statutory criminal-proceeding suspension excludes interest for its suspension period. The taxpayer submits the calculation for authority verification/approval under 176(4). Use the [pack's sourced 2026 benchmark calculation](moldova-vat.md#penalties-and-interest) and actual due/refund dates; do not assume interest is paid automatically. [Code 176(1),(3)–(4); HG93 point 51](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=157050&lang=ro).

rows.old_text: ## Cross-border points
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Foreign currency receipts and an overseas address do not establish an export exemption. Obtain the place-of-supply conclusion and recipient evidence from the [VAT Guide](moldova-vat.md), then the route-specific HG93 point 32 proof above. Keep customs/import VAT payment evidence distinct from an overseas supplier payment. Zone/port/airport claims depend on actual resident status, the elected customs guarantee regime and the evidence in point 32(11). Cross-Nistru and treaty/project-specific implementing questions remain under Sources; a foreign transfer is not sufficient proof.

rows.old_text: ## Two worked examples that recompute
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### 1. Official ordinary export cap and paid-credit order
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Recompute HG93 annex 2¹: domestic output VAT 2,000; export value 6,000 with standard-rate cap 1,200; current input 1,000, of which 800 paid/200 unpaid; opening credit 2,500, of which 500 paid/2,000 unpaid. All eligibility/proof assumptions are those stated in the official annex, not a claim that a particular taxpayer qualifies. Allocate output against 2,200 unpaid first. The remaining paid credit is 1,300 and total excess 1,500; refund 1,200, leaving paid 100/unpaid 200. [Official annex 2¹](https://www.legis.md/UserFiles/Image/RO/2024/mo%20564-568%20ro/an_2_1_93_MD.docx).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text:
```oa-check
name: Moldova official export refund paid-unpaid order
tolerance: 0.0001
inputs:
  output_vat: 2000
  export_value: 6000
  current_paid: 800
  current_unpaid: 200
  opening_paid: 500
  opening_unpaid: 2000
steps:
  total_paid: current_paid + opening_paid
  total_unpaid: current_unpaid + opening_unpaid
  output_against_unpaid: min(output_vat, total_unpaid)
  unpaid_left: total_unpaid - output_against_unpaid
  paid_left: total_paid - max(output_vat - total_unpaid, 0)
  excess: total_paid + total_unpaid - output_vat
  supply_cap: export_value * 0.20
  refund: min(excess, paid_left, supply_cap)
  paid_carry: paid_left - refund
  total_carry: excess - refund
expected:
  output_against_unpaid: 2000
  unpaid_left: 200
  paid_left: 1300
  excess: 1500
  supply_cap: 1200
  refund: 1200
  paid_carry: 100
  total_carry: 300
```

rows.old_text: ### 2. Qualifying e-Factura excess, arrears and bank balance
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Hypothetical wholly eligible Code 101⁶ month after January 2023: qualifying system-documented output VAT 10,000; eligible input VAT actually paid at application 25,000; no unpaid or December 2022 credits, other adjustments or previous refunds. The paid excess is 15,000 but the 70% output cap is 7,000. Assume SFS confirms that amount, with 1,500 actual taxpayer arrears and no future-tax allocation. Offset 1,500 and bank 5,500; carry 8,000 remains. Bank receipt still requires Treasury evidence. [HG93 point 47³; Code 101⁶(2),(4); approved annex 1](https://www.legis.md/cautare/getResults?doc_id=152472&lang=ro).
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

```oa-check
name: Moldova e-Factura refund cap and settlement
tolerance: 0.0001
inputs:
  paid_input: 25000
  qualifying_output: 10000
  arrears: 1500
steps:
  paid_excess: paid_input - qualifying_output
  programme_cap: qualifying_output * 0.70
  confirmed_refund: min(paid_excess, programme_cap)
  offset: min(confirmed_refund, arrears)
  bank_instruction: confirmed_refund - offset
  carry_forward: paid_excess - confirmed_refund
expected:
  paid_excess: 15000
  programme_cap: 7000
  confirmed_refund: 7000
  offset: 1500
  bank_instruction: 5500
  carry_forward: 8000
```

rows.old_text: ### Ordinary annual income and registered business/professional profit
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text:
1. Establish residence/citizenship, source, legal activity, year and regime. Separate final-withholding income, exempt receipts, non-business annual income, business profit and special-regime turnover. Do not tax every bank credit or apply 12% to every activity labelled “freelance”. [Arts. 13–15, 18–21, 69^1–69^26, 90^1][code].
2. Apply the proper timing method. Non-business individuals ordinarily use cash accounting. Individual entrepreneurs can use cash or accrual under art. 44; professional-sector individual taxpayers use the specified cash method under art. 69^2, while legal entities use accrual. Do not deduct an unpaid expense simply because an invoice exists under a cash method, and do not ignore accrued income under an accrual method. Method changes require the statutory adjustment to avoid omissions/double counting. [Arts. 44, 69^2][code].
3. Include the taxable business/professional receipts, salary, rent, interest, royalties, covered debt releases, subsidies and other art. 18 sources under their applicable regime. Exclude only the exact art. 20 category and person entitled to it. State social benefits, qualifying damages/donations/inheritances, contributions to capital, specified grants and other exemptions have different conditions. Foreign payer, grant, gift or private-transfer wording alone is not the exemption. [Arts. 18–21][code].
4. For ordinary business/professional income, deduct actual ordinary necessary business expenditure under the applicable chapter-3 rules and accounting method. Preserve invoices, contract, business purpose, payment/timing and apportionment. Mixed business/private costs require art. 24(2)'s greater-business-than-private test and only the direct business portion. No default home-office, phone/internet, car, meal or travel percentage is certified. Capital purchases, private expenses, income tax, statutory fines/penalties and exempt-income costs cannot all be deducted as ordinary expenses. [Arts. 24–31, 44, 69^3][code].
5. Keep operating expenses separate from deductible personal mandatory contributions and personal allowances. Article 35^2(1)–(2) allows actual compulsory medical and social contributions paid by the person in statutory amounts during the period. The employer's social cost is not the employee's payment. Do not deduct the same premium in business expenses and again as a personal deduction. The ordinary employee 6% social deduction in the old Guide is removed. Use the actual fixed category and payments rather than assigning every self-payer the same amount. [Art. 35^2][code]; [CNAS 2026 categories][cnas]; [CET18 instruction points 33–34][cet].
6. For qualifying ordinary business tax losses, keep the article-32 origin-year ledger, following five periods, remaining amounts and chronological use. Capital losses are restricted separately to capital gains; special turnover taxes do not become profit taxes through an expense/loss deduction. Do not transfer a business loss into every household income category. [Arts. 32, 40–41, 54^2, 69^10, 69^24][code].
7. Apply actual exemptions and personal deductions only once. Compute ordinary tax at the applicable legal rate, then match allowable creditable domestic withholding/instalments and foreign-tax credit to the same taxable income/period. Final art. 90^1 withholding is not a general credit against ordinary tax. Separate an amount payable from an excess payment/refund request. [Arts. 15–16, 33–35^2, 79, 81–87, 90^1][code].

rows.old_text: For expenses, preserve the original Guide's practical categories as evidence questions: software/cloud/SaaS and platform charges; telecom/utilities; home office/rent; travel/transport; banking/professional charges; subcontractors; equipment/capital assets; private expenditure and mixed use. Vendor names such as a software supplier or airline do not establish a deduction or the VAT result. For an asset with life above one year and value above 12,000, test the tangible depreciation regime, separate asset register, commencement, Government life and permitted method. The non-financial accelerated option is a maximum first-year 50% under its conditions, not a universal write-off. Bad debt requires the statutory compromised-debt proof; an uncollected cash-basis receipt never taxed does not automatically create a tax deduction. Interest benchmarks, one-car occupation limits, business-charity caps and supporting procedures require their actual statutory facts. [Arts. 24–26^1, 28, 31–32, 36, 44][code]; [corporate method and remaining procedure gaps](md-corporate-income-tax.md).

Article 21(3) defines transaction-date evidence, year-end debt revaluation, advances and uncoted-currency conversion. Preserve gross foreign receipts, fees, withholding, original currency, bank/platform dates and the applicable official rate independently. Match the actual accounting method and current-year FX differences rather than treating every bank conversion difference as a deductible cost. [Art. 21(3)][code].

Article 21(4) deems excess cash donations by a non-business donor income to that donor over the period's income, subject to the first-degree relative/affinity and spouse exceptions. Article 40 has its separate donated-capital-asset treatment; recipient exemptions under art. 20 have their own citizenship/category conditions. Internal transfers and loan principal are reconciliation subjects, not automatically business income or an automatic tax exemption for an unexplained receipt. [Arts. 20–21, 40][code].

The companion’s foreign-currency and collection/rounding gaps remain applicable; this annual-income Guide does not turn the loan principal into salary. rows.old_text: ### Personal, spouse and dependent exemptions
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For the personal exemption, including the increased art. 33(2) amount, verify the resident's statutory annual taxable-income test strictly below 360,000, excluding art. 90^1 income and taking account of the specified chapter-10^2/10^3 income. Exactly 360,000 fails a “less than” test. Do not use only salary or blindly multiply the latest net/gross bank payment by twelve. The employer is not required to track the employee's loss of entitlement under art. 88(1); annual reconciliation remains necessary. [Arts. 33(1)–(2), 83, 88][code]; [Government Decision 693/2018 annex 2 point 21^1][personalreg].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The increased personal amount requires the exact listed Chernobyl/qualifying war/disability or rehabilitated-repression category and evidence. The spouse relief requires a spouse in art. 33(2)'s category who is not using the personal exemption; it is not a standard allowance transferable by every couple. The dependent must meet the cumulative relationship and income requirements, including the specified guardian/curator route; the annual 12,400 income test excludes only the specified State disability allowances. Dependents' age alone does not answer the relationship/income test. Spouse/dependent rights arise from the next month under arts. 34–35. The current regulation applies the personal-exemption annual-income gate to art. 33 and expressly preserves the separate art. 34–35 spouse/dependent tests. The increased personal amount is not an exception to that gate. The personal exemption and dependent/spouse routes must be tested separately. [Annex 2 point 21^1][personalreg]. [Arts. 33–35][code]; [payroll regulation points 9–35 and evidence tables][reg].

No valid claim/evidence means no payroll exemptions; a mid-year hire does not automatically receive twelve months. The annual twelfths are 2,475 standard, 2,885 increased and 825/1,815 for the relevant dependent/spouse categories in eligible months. Special-regime months restrict relief under art. 35^1; the regulation has the separate mixed-month rule. Annual claims, newly acquired residence, divorce, death, maternity and a dependent's income changes need their own reconciliation, not a permanent default amount. [Arts. 34–35^1, 88][code]; [regulation points 9–26, 38–48][reg]; [payroll method](moldova-payroll.md).

rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Article 35^2 permits actual mandatory health premiums and mandatory social contributions paid within the legal amounts. Its separate personal routes cover voluntary medical insurance or qualifying medical services from one provider for an insured person; covered life/health/fire/natural-disaster insurance contracts with the stated combined cap; and interest paid for the first home on a qualifying non-State-programme credit, apportioned by ownership share for jointly owned property. The forecast-salary cap is 17,400 for the stated 2026 routes. Do not create two independent medical caps merely because CET18 has separate E3/E4 fields, deduct a loan's principal as home-loan interest, or deduct a premium paid by somebody else as this person's expenditure. [Art. 35^2(1)–(5)][code]; [CNAS point 12.1][cnas]; [CET18 points 33–35^1][cet].

The January 2026 version explicitly records this change operative 1 January. Retain provider, beneficiary, contract/invoice and payment evidence. Current CET18 point 34^6 refers to this Code amount, but generic point 34^7 still says one forecast salary for E3–E7. Follow the statute's 20,000 for the 2026 education working paper and record the inconsistency; do not reduce the legal cap to 17,400 or certify the portal's 2026 filing implementation without checking it. The directly read Government proof requirements and January/June change are set out below; the separate current form/portal inconsistency is not certified as resolved. rows.old_text: ### Capital gains, property and financial receipts
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Identify the capital asset and the type/date of disposal. Article 39 covers the specified participation/debt/property/land/option assets. Under art. 40, gross monetary/non-monetary disposal value less documented adjusted cost produces each recognised gain/loss. Use the broker report for the specified exchange transactions. Only 50% of recognised gains above recognised current-period losses enters the income base; capital losses cannot reduce unrelated ordinary income. Do not apply 12% to the full sale proceeds or assume every investment gain is finally withheld. [Arts. 39–42][code]; [CET18 capital table K, points 60–67][cet].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Cost must be established under art. 42 and the applicable documentation rule. Purchase/self-build, gifts/inheritance/lifetime maintenance, exchanges, privatisation, contributions to capital and stock-option awards have different bases. The statute includes zero cost where supporting documents are absent, with its specific self-constructed-property cadastral route rather than an invented estimate. Keep capital changes and historical ownership records; an untaxed receipt's market value is not automatically the cost of every asset. [Art. 42][code].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: **Allocate proceeds and cost before applying the 50% inclusion.** Government Decision 693/2018 annex 2 point 39 allocates a single acquisition price among multiple capital assets in proportion to each asset's market value on the transaction date. Under point 40, jointly owned disposal proceeds **and adjusted cost** follow each owner's share; for undivided common ownership, the written common agreement identifies one owner as the taxpayer under that route. Do not allocate only proceeds, use the full joint cost for every owner, or infer that a written reporting agreement changes every substantive ownership rule. [Code arts. 40–42][code]; [annex 2 points 38–40][personalreg].

Keep cumulative proceeds and cost already used so the same full basis is not deducted against every instalment. Point 43 separately states an arithmetic-average basis for the specified differently valued equity/debt/ownership positions in the same business; do not invent a universal FIFO or apply that paragraph to unrelated property. Post-1998 capital contributions use the documented monetary contribution, including subsequent contributions; older property/shares have their own 1 January 1998/31 December 1997 basis provisions. Adjust actual capital withdrawals/increases under Code art. 42(4). [Code art. 42][code]; [annex 2 points 41–44][personalreg].

rows.old_text: **Obtain the correct cost documents.** MF Order 40/2018 approves the capital-cost proof list; its complete annex has now been retained and read, with the nine-route document map below. For inherited property, the SFS's published Order 13/2025 interpretation, question 29.2.4.18, confirms the legal-heir certificate together with either a competent valuation report establishing market value on acquisition, or the property-value certificate from the State property-register authority. rows.old_text: Use **current Code 264’s statutory start dates**, rather than the actual date a late return/payment was made. Under 264(1)(a), tax and late charges can be determined within **four years from the last statutory filing date**, or the payment due date if no return is prescribed. Tax-specific sanctions use the corresponding statutory filing/payment date under 264(1)(b); sanctions unrelated to a particular tax use the offence date under 264(1)(c). Paragraph 2 is repealed. Under 264(3), SFS can extend the period subject to control, **not beyond six years from the last statutory filing date**, where no return was submitted or the taxpayer seeks an overpayment/statutory refund. The suspension list covers the stated detention/absence, deferral/instalment, court, insolvency, special-record and enforcement circumstances. - Supply gross income by category/source/date, foreign currency and fees, withholding certificates, business invoices/expenses, accounting method and actual payments. Identify own-account transfers, loans, gifts, benefits and property transactions separately.
- Supply personal/spouse/dependent evidence and dates, signed payroll applications/non-use, annual-income facts, actual compulsory contributions and medical/insurance/home-interest/education payment/provider documents.
- Supply asset cost/ownership/main-home records, disposal proceeds, broker reports, gains/losses and certified foreign taxes for the same taxed income/period.
- Supply accepted returns/notices, instalments/withholding, SFS/CNAS/CNAM account statements, payment/refund receipts and any corrections or assessments. Do not finalise from bank totals alone.

rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ## Who this applies to
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Compute Moldova's 2026 ordinary employment withholding, employer social contributions and employee medical premiums using the employee's actual status, gross components, accrual period, payment dates and exemption application. This is a source-cited draft. The bounded source-review record is linked under Sources; accountant attestation is not provided. [Fiscal Code arts. 15, 19, 88][code]; [Government Decision 697/2014, 2026 regulation][reg].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Article 88 also treats covered work/service payments to individuals not carrying on business, board/audit-commission remuneration and administrator mandates through its employment-income rules. The regulation covers day workers, student trainees and dual-education learners as specified. Day workers cannot claim the chapter-4 exemptions. Registered independent service entrepreneurs have a separate single tax, but art. 88(8) treats their relations with counterparties outside art. 24(11^1)'s conditions as employment for tax purposes. Registration or an invoice alone does not settle that test. [Arts. 15(a^1), 24(11^1), 88(5)–(8)][code]; [regulation points 1–6, 9^2][reg].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Choose the employer social category independently: ordinary private/commercial and specified higher-education/medical employers; budgetary/public institutions; listed special-condition aviation; qualifying agriculture; or the actual special regime. A general hazardous-work description does not prove a 32% rate. Ordinary payroll has no additional 6% employee social withholding under the listed employer tariffs. The old Guide's employee 6% deduction and 27%-of-gross “combined employee rate” are corrected here. [CNAS instructions points 9–13][cnas]; [Law 489 art. 17][social].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: IT-park salary, the historical/sector software-worker rules referenced by the regulation, and fixed/self-payer contributions need their actual regime and dates. IT-park status does not exempt every civil-service contract, and the accrued-versus-paid transition rules matter when entering/leaving the park regime. See [social/medical contributions](moldova-social-contributions.md) for the full category map and its remaining gaps, and [individual income tax](moldova-income-tax.md) for annual liability and final withholding. This Guide is not a labour-law calculation of contractual wage, paid leave, sickness entitlement or severance. Establish those amounts from the applicable documents/law before taxing them. [Law 489 art. 19(7)][social]; [regulation points 5, 36^1, 39][reg].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Both the January and current Code retain the cited personal/spouse/dependent amounts and the strict personal-exemption gate. At exactly 360,000, do not apply a rule written as “less than”. Do not substitute annualised contractual gross alone for the statutory annual-income test. Dependent/spouse relief has its own conditions; loss of the standard personal exemption does not automatically erase every other documented exemption. The employer is not obliged to track loss of the personal-exemption right; the employee's annual liability and application duties remain separate. [Arts. 33–35, 88(1)][code]; [regulation points 10^1, 16][reg].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ## The base
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Build separate payroll, contribution and payment records
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Record the employer's registration/activity/category, worker identity, contractual and actual status, actual hours and dates, accrual month, each taxable payment, gross cash, benefits, excluded amounts and supporting law. Maintain separate bases for PIT, social insurance and medical insurance. Do not treat every meal ticket or reimbursement as taxable under every system. The amounts “calculated”, “directed to payment”, “paid”, “insured income” and “net bank transfer” serve different purposes. [Code arts. 18–20, 88][code]; [Law 489 arts. 20, 22–23][social]; [Law 1593 arts. 3–6, 20][health]; [IPC21 tables 1–2][ipc].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: PIT includes covered salary, bonus, commission, fees, taxable material assistance and non-cash benefits, less only the deductions/exemptions actually available. Exclusions require the precise art. 20 category and relevant art. 24/Government limits. A vendor name or an accounting description is not an exemption. Keep business travel, transport/food/training, gifts, medical benefits, childcare, vouchers and other reimbursements separately identified. The [corporate Guide](md-corporate-income-tax.md) records the underlying employee-benefit caps and its Government-procedure gaps; do not silently treat an unresolved cap as unlimited. [Code arts. 18(c), 19–20, 24][code]; [regulation points 3, 6–8][reg].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: For benefits, establish the actual valuation rule. Taxable benefits include personal-expense reimbursements and payments to third parties, the excess nominal meal-ticket value, specified trainee transport/food over the allowed amount, forgiven employee debt, covered housing top-ups, concessional loans and employer property used personally. For an employer-owned asset, art. 19(e) uses the statutory daily percentage and starting tax-undepreciated value rather than a guessed rental price; non-owned assets use the employer's actual daily right-of-use cost. A below-cost employee charge leaves the difference as a benefit under regulation point 8(5). For concessional loans, compare the actual employee rate with the preceding-November BNM weighted new individual-loan rate for terms above five years; the banking/non-bank-lender ordinary-customer exception has its own facts. The ordinary MDL benchmark and observed loan/day formula are supplied below; the stated foreign-currency and implementation limits remain. [Art. 19][code]; [regulation points 7–8][reg].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: **Employer-loan benefit, ordinary MDL case.** Current Code art. 19(d) selects the preceding-November BNM weighted rate for **new loans to individuals with a term over five years**. It does not select the employer's own bank cost, the all-bank/all-term total, the individual-entrepreneur series or the 6% monetary-policy base used for late charges. The configured BNM DPMC8 report for **November 2025**, `moneda naţională → persoane fizice: total → peste 5 ani → Rata nominală,%`, shows **8.32%**. The current statutory paragraph does not direct rounding this benchmark up to 9%. Retain the exact report period, currency, borrower group and maturity row, since the report opens at its latest period by default. [Code art. 19(d)][code]; [configured BNM loan report][loanreport].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The formula image embedded in current regulation point 8(4) was visually read: `F = S × (Nzl / 365) × ((Rd − Rdc) / 100)`. `F` is the benefit, `S` the loan balance, `Nzl` the days of use in the month, `Rd` the BNM benchmark and `Rdc` the employee loan rate, with rates expressed as percentages. Apply the Code's **positive-difference** rule: a benchmark-minus-contract-rate result at or below zero produces no positive interest benefit. For the ordinary MDL case, calculate each established balance segment as `balance × use_days / 365 × max(0, 8.32 − actual_employee_rate_percent) / 100`, then total the month's segments. Do not divide an annual benefit by twelve irrespective of days, use the full original principal after repayment, or create a negative taxable benefit. [Code art. 19(d)][code]; [regulation point 8(4), monthly determination and repayments][reg]; [official formula image][loanformula].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The regulation requires monthly determination and recalculation for principal repayments; it also applies the stated method to loans granted and still unpaid in periods through 2019. Obtain the actual agreement, disbursement/balance and rate histories, repayment allocation and days of use. The bank/non-bank-lender exception requires the same financial product on general conditions accepted for **at least one third-party individual**; employment by a lender alone is insufficient. Keep loan principal, actual interest and the deemed benefit separate. Feed the benefit into the applicable cumulative PIT calculation; this value-only method does not establish every contribution-base exclusion, actual cash withholding or a no-cash-wages remittance route. Foreign-currency/FX-linked benchmark selection, no-observation rows, conversion and precise transaction-day/final monetary-rounding conventions remain explicit gaps. A published foreign-currency row showing zero rate **and zero volume** is not treated as proof of a universal zero employee-loan benchmark. [Code arts. 19(d), 88][code]; [regulation points 8(4), 38–44][reg]; [BNM report currency/borrower/term data and notes][loanreport].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Social contributions use the covered accrued salary/remuneration base and the employer's statutory category. Compare the actual base with the national minimum proportionate to time worked and, for part-time/reduced work, the separate minimum contribution of one quarter of the full-minimum contribution. Do not deduct the employer's contribution from the employee's cash. Agriculture's State 6% is not an employer outlay or employee withholding. Special aviation and public rates are not general substitutes for 24%. [Law 489 arts. 17, 20, 22–23][social]; [CNAS points 9–13][cnas].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Medical premiums ordinarily apply to covered gross before PIT or other deductions, and follow the actual remuneration payment timing. Excluded remuneration and IT-park salary require their own statutory tests. Do not import the social minimum floor into the employee's medical base. A payment in 2026 for remuneration through 31 December 2020 has IPC21 instruction point 9's specific historical health-premium rule; the ordinary current-payroll percentage summary is not a historical-period calculation. [Law 1593 arts. 3–6, 12, 20][health]; [medical budget art. 4][medicalbudget]; [IPC21 instruction point 9][ipc].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ### Establish exemptions from applications and evidence
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Obtain the signed application and current supporting evidence, including residence, disability/qualifying category, marriage and spouse non-use, dependent relationship/identity/income and guardian status where relevant. Use regulation points 30–35 and its tables for the document requirements and exemption codes P, M, Sm, Nx and Hx. The old blanket refusal “missing IDNP means never file” is replaced by the actual IPC21 identity rule in the filing section. A taxpayer identification record, an exemption application and a social-insurance record are different evidence. [Code art. 88(2)–(4)][code]; [regulation points 17, 30–35][reg].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: A resident can use exemptions at the main employment, secondary employment, service payer or dual-education location as permitted, but cannot duplicate the personal exemption for the same period at another place. Day workers receive no chapter-4 exemptions. A general family or disability label is not enough. Qualifying spouse relief is whole rather than divided between spouses; divorce requires the stated annual recalculation. Dependents must meet art. 35's cumulative relationship and income conditions, with the specified guardian/curator route and disability allowances excluded from the income test. If the application or supporting documents are missing, incomplete or withdrawn, withhold **without exemptions** under point 21; do not default to the standard personal amount. Residence acquired mid-year has the separate application/annual-return route, not an automatic employer recalculation from January. Special-regime months, mixed standard/special months, death and spouse/dependent changes have their own provisions. [Code art. 88(2)–(3)][code]; [regulation points 16^1–26, 38][reg].

rows.old_text: ### Compute PIT cumulatively and reconcile the current payment
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text:
1. Establish the start of the current-year employment/covered relationship and the applicable payment-year rules. For December salary paid in January, regulation point 29 uses the rate/exemptions at payment. This does not change the separate social accrual and insured-period record.
2. For each payment, keep cumulative taxable gross and taxable benefits, deductible medical premiums and other verified payroll deductions, and the cumulative exemptions for eligible months. Determine taxable cumulative income after these deductions/exemptions, without inventing an employee 6% social deduction. Article 35^2 permits actual mandatory personal contributions under its own conditions; the employer's contribution is not that personal payment. Other annual personal deductions require their actual legal/reporting route rather than an assumed monthly allowance.
3. Calculate cumulative ordinary PIT at 12% and compare with PIT already withheld this year from the same relationship. Current withholding is the difference required by the cumulative record. Separate payments and advances within the same month do not each receive another month's exemption. A negative adjustment/refund has the regulation's correction method; do not blindly floor the withholding difference to zero and lose a genuine overpayment.
4. Reconcile the amount of PIT/medical withheld, other lawful deductions and actual net cash. Employer cost is gross plus employer social and any actual additional employer cost, not an automatic employee tax gross-up. Keep non-cash benefits and prior advances separately so they are not paid in cash twice.
5. Reconcile nominal insured periods/contributions, the payment-period PIT/medical report, employee personal record and treasury payments. Keep proof of filing acceptance and allocation, not merely a screenshot of a submitted draft.

rows.old_text: Assume an ordinary private employer, a full month, covered gross accrued and paid 17,400, no taxable non-cash benefit/other deduction, and an employee continuing from the prior year with a valid prior application giving the January standard personal exemption. The statutory annual-income test is satisfied and no exemption is duplicated. Medical is 1,566; the month's exemption is 2,475; ordinary PIT base is 13,359 and PIT 1,603.08. Net cash is 14,230.92. ```oa-check
name: Moldova 2026 continuing employee January cumulative payroll
inputs:
  gross: 17400
  medical_rate: 0.09
  annual_personal_exemption: 29700
  eligible_months: 1
  pit_rate: 0.12
  employer_social_rate: 0.24
  prior_pit: 0
steps:
  medical: gross * medical_rate
  cumulative_exemption: annual_personal_exemption / 12 * eligible_months
  cumulative_taxable: max(0, gross - medical - cumulative_exemption)

  current_pit: cumulative_pit - prior_pit
  net_cash: gross - medical - current_pit
  employer_social: gross * employer_social_rate
  employer_cost: gross + employer_social

Keep one March exemption of 2,475, not one per payment. At the second payment, cumulative taxable income is 15,725 and PIT 1,887; withhold a further 655.20. March total PIT is 795, medical 900 and net 8,305. rows.old_text: # Moldova social contributions and medical insurance, 2026 v0.14
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: ## Who this applies to
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Determine the actual payer category, insured person, remuneration, work period and payment date before calculating Moldova's 2026 social contributions or mandatory medical insurance. These are different systems with different bases and timing. This source-cited draft replaces the earlier mixed-year summary. It has a bounded source-review record linked under Sources and is not accountant-attested; the country remains partial. [Law 489/1999 arts. 17–23][social]; [Law 1593/2002][health].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Social insurance covers the ordinary private and public employer categories, specified special-condition work, IT-park employment, independent family physicians, qualifying agriculture, individual/farm founders, independent retail and plant-product purchasing, justice professions, patents, day workers and the new independent service entrepreneurs. A sole trader, patent holder and independent service entrepreneur are not interchangeable categories. Obtain actual registration and overlapping employment/pension/disability records. Insured benefits also differ by category; payment of a fixed amount does not establish entitlement to every benefit. [Law 489 art. 17 and annex 1; CNAS instructions points 2–3, 10–20][instructions].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Mandatory health insurance separately distinguishes percentage payers in Law 1593 annex 1 and fixed-premium categories in annex 2. Current annex 1 identifies employees as percentage payers and includes the covered civil-contract remuneration route. Do not recreate an employer/employee percentage split from an older summary. For IT-park salary, use the special single-tax route; civil-contract payments remain a separate classification. State-insured status, concurrent categories, residence and the dates a status starts or ends matter. [Law 1593 arts. 4–6 and annexes 1–2][health]; [2026 medical budget art. 4][medicalbudget].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Foreign citizenship alone does not exempt a worker from social insurance. Law 489 art. 19(6) applies the charging rule to the stated national/foreign/stateless groups and contains a specific exception for foreigners meeting Law 200/2010 art. 43^17 conditions. Establish those conditions or the operative international agreement before claiming an exemption. Tax residence and social-insurance coverage require separate legal tests. [Law 489 art. 19(6)][social].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: Use [payroll](moldova-payroll.md) for wage withholding and net pay and [individual income tax](moldova-income-tax.md) for annual residence, allowances, investment income and returns. Their remaining ordinary gaps stay explicit in the country README. Bank descriptions, the old Guide's “Tier 1/Tier 2” rule headings and a matching payment amount do not establish legal eligibility or review status.
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: All amounts are MDL. Classify first; the same percentage does not make two categories equivalent. CNAS instructions below are the authority's 2026 operating instructions, Order 31-A of 18 February 2026, with their cited statutory provisions. The actual current annex-1 tariff DOCX has now been downloaded, retained and read; its benefit classes and category payment clocks are set out below.

rows.old_text: ### What the actual tariff annex covers
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The current Law 489 annex 1 directly confirms each tariff category, its payment clock and insured-benefit population. Rows 1.1–1.5 cover the stated ordinary, special-condition, physician, IT-park and agricultural classes; their ordinary monthly deadline is the 25th of the following month. The agricultural 24% row splits into employer 18% and State 6%. Row 1.1 also includes the stated IT-park civil work/service contracts and internationally funded employment subject to its agreement exception; neither employer label alone proves exemption. [Actual annex 1 rows 1.1–1.5][socialtariff].

The annex delegates the fixed amounts to the annual budget; use the separately sourced 2026 amounts above and the category/start/cessation rules below. Do not import the justice-profession benefit class into founder/patent/day-worker categories, or revive the former taxi fixed category after its sourced transition. [Actual annex 1 rows 1.6–1.10][socialtariff]; [2026 social budget art.3][socialbudget]; [CNAS category instructions][instructions].

rows.old_text: ### Ordinary social contribution and the minimum
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text:
1. Establish the statutory employer and worker category. Do not choose 24%, 29%, 32% or 39% from the bank reference or assume that all difficult/hazardous jobs are civil-aviation special-condition jobs. Annex 2 lists navigant, air-traffic and technical aviation roles; apply the actual category and documented conditions. The ordinary employer contribution is an employer cost, separate from the employee health deduction and PIT. [Law 489 arts. 17–18, annex 2][social]; [CNAS points 9–10][instructions].
2. Reconcile accrued gross salary and other covered remuneration for every employee to the payroll and nominal insured record. Social contributions follow accrual/calculation, not merely the date cash leaves the bank. A wage bank debit often represents net cash after withholding and does not identify the social base. [Law 489 art. 20(1), (5)][social]; [CNAS points 5–9][instructions].
3. Apply Law 489 art. 22(1)'s minimum: the employee's monthly base cannot be lower than the national minimum in proportion to time worked. For part-time or reduced work, the calculated social contribution cannot be below 25% of the contribution on the full national monthly minimum. Compare the actual contribution, the time-proportionate minimum contribution and that separate floor. Obtain the actual time/work-status record; do not impose an ordinary-salary calculation on an IT-park insured-income entry or a fixed-tax category. The minimum wording is present in both the January and current selected statute. [Art. 22][social]; [January art. 22][socialjan].
4. For amounts calculated now for other service periods, preserve both the calculation/reporting month and the actual insured service periods. CNAS points 7–8.3 apply the calculation-period tariff and current reporting method; their December/January holiday-pay and employer/state-funded sickness examples require distinct nominal categories. Do not shift every prior-year correction into a fictional current service period. Historical declaration corrections have their own rules below. [CNAS points 7–8.3, 33][instructions].
5. Test every excluded payment against Law 489 annex 3. Exclusion from PIT or a corporate deduction is not automatically exclusion from social insurance. Excluded remuneration also does not enter the insured-benefit calculation under art. 23(2). [Law 489 art. 23 and annex 3][social].
rows.status: Retained byte-exact in existing Guide; the two new methods are additions, not rewrites.

rows.old_text: The following statutory exclusion groups preserve ordinary remuneration distinctions. Apply the exact facts and any cited Government procedure; the label alone is insufficient. Annex 3 covers Government-organised transport/food/training and student-trainee transport/food; duty-travel and specified injury compensation; statutory redundancy amounts; specified public/military service compensation; protection equipment, therapeutic food and the stated treatment/rest facilities; qualifying gifts and Fiscal Code art. 24(19^3)/(20) payments; scholarships and specified student work; duty-transfer travel/removal/housing; the stated young-specialist payments; temporary-incapacity benefits and public-budget social benefits; property-management income including dividends/interest; state-bond proceeds; qualifying grants; copyright and civil-agreement amounts **except work/service contracts**; inventions; qualifying union/employer-organisation material aid; specified injury/death compensation; sport/competition awards; survey participation rewards; damage compensation **except salary for forced absence**; patent activity receipts; specified state first-home/teacher payments; SARS-CoV-2 testing/vaccination; alternative childcare up to 2,500 monthly per employee's child under 3; and the stated electoral-worker indemnity. Public/medical staff commuting/housing and strategic-industry young-worker payments have their own exact conditions. This is a classification map, not a universal exemption for every payment with one of these names. [Law 489 annex 3 points 1–43][social].

These correspond to Law 1593 art. 23(4)–(5): the patent overlap for art. 4(4)(i),(j), and the agricultural-landowner exemption for concurrent State coverage or proven presence abroad exceeding 183 calendar days during the budget year. rows.old_text: For employees, CNAM uses the SFS employment-information route, including IRM19, and status follows the start/end or qualifying suspension of employment. Law 1585 art. 6(4)(i) preserves the specified suspension exceptions for circumstances outside the parties' will, medical-certificate leave to care for an ill family member up to two years, and partially paid childcare leave until age 3. Fixed-premium status ordinarily starts on payment of the required premium/associated late charge and is suspended on **31 January of the following year**, with the specified maternity/childcare exception. A fixed payer suspending activity for maternity or partially paid childcare leave until age 3 supplies an application, the activity-suspension decision and the medical/birth certificate under Regulation point 18^3. The two-year State-insured mother category and three-year leave exception are distinct rules. [Law 1585 art. 6(4)–(6)][healthframework]; [Regulation 1246 points 14, 18^3, 21, 34][healthstatus].
